userStories.title: 25 FAQ answers were asserted in structured data and present on no page
userStories.description:
Five pages render their FAQ as an accordion whose panel was written `{isOpen &&

{answer}

}`. Conditional mounting means a closed accordion has no answer text in the document at all — not hidden, absent — and the prerender snapshots the closed state. So the homepage, /pricing, both blog category pages and two feature pages shipped FAQPage JSON-LD asserting 25 answers that appear nowhere in the HTML those pages serve. Google's FAQPage requirement is that the answer be present on the page; an accordion is explicitly allowed, and not rendering the content is not the same thing. On /features/analytics and /features/lead-capture the same block also carried itemProp='text' microdata describing an element that did not exist. The audit has checked since US-157 that FAQ questions are visible, and every question was — which is why this survived: the question and the answer are separate assertions and only one of them was being checked.
acceptanceCriteria: Every answer in FAQPage JSON-LD appears in the HTML of the page that asserts it
The accordions still collapse — the answer is hidden, not unmounted
verify:seo checks answers as well as questions, demonstrated failing on the build as it shipped
The rule accepts an answer that is present but hidden, because that is what an accordion is
userStories.notes: Done 2026-09-10, iteration 14 of the SEO loop. `hidden` rather than a CSS class: it is the platform attribute for 'in the document, not painted', it needs no stylesheet to work during a prerender, and it is what assistive technology already understands alongside the aria-expanded these buttons carry. The test that matters is the one asserting the question check still PASSES on the broken fixture — that is the reason 25 answers went unnoticed through six earlier audits of this same schema type.

userStories.title: CI ran every SEO check against a build with no blog in it
userStories.description: CI's build job sets PRERENDER_ALLOW_NO_ARTICLES=1, because it has no database credentials, and that flag omitted the blog routes entirely. So `npm run verify:seo` — page identity (US-150), sitemap reachability (US-165), structured-data URLs (US-179), internal links (US-184), FAQ question and answer visibility (US-157/US-185) — ran against the marketing pages and never once looked at /blog, /blog/category/{slug} or /blog/{slug}. That is where the defects were: US-184's six broken category links were on /blog, US-180's fabricated Person author was on every article, and eight of US-185's 25 missing FAQ answers were on the two category pages. None of those regressions could have been caught by CI, because CI did not build the pages they were on.
acceptanceCriteria: A database-less verification build renders the blog, so every check covers it
The articles it renders are unmistakably fixtures, in their title and their first sentence
A build that intends to deploy cannot reach the fixture, even by mistake
The fixture covers the branches that only the blog has: an article with a foreign featured image, one without, and one in a category the registry does not list
CI's comments say what the flag now does
userStories.notes: Done 2026-09-10, iteration 15 and last of the SEO loop. No new flag: PRERENDER_ALLOW_NO_ARTICLES already means 'this build will not ship', and a deploy is already forbidden from setting it, so changing what it DOES from 'omit the blog' to 'render three fixtures' adds coverage without widening the blast radius. loadFixtureArticles() is deliberately not reachable from loadArticles(): a build that intends to deploy must never silently fall back to invented content, which is the argument of US-169 and is why the real snapshot is still uncommitted. The loader refuses any fixture whose title does not begin 'Fixture:' — if one of these ever escaped, it should be obvious in the first line rather than plausible.

form-vendor leaves the first-paint critical path: 253.97 kB gzip of eager chunks becomes 222.72 kB, a 31.25 kB (12.3%) saving on every first load

userStories.title: The SSRF guard was bypassable, and its test passed
userStories.description: As the operator of a platform whose edge functions fetch caller-supplied URLs while holding the service-role key, I need the guard to refuse a private address in every encoding the URL parser can produce, not only in the one a person would type.
acceptanceCriteria: isBlockedAddress expands an IPv6 address to its eight groups instead of pattern-matching text
Every form that embeds an IPv4 address is read and checked: mapped (::ffff:0:0/96), compatible (::/96), NAT64 (64:ff9b::/96) and 6to4 (2002::/16)
An address that cannot be parsed is refused, not treated as public
A zone index (fe80::1%eth0) does not defeat the link-local check
The tests use the literal output of new URL(...).hostname, because that is what the guard is handed
The new tests are verified against the shipped implementation: 6 of them fail there
userStories.notes: Found in iteration 9. new URL() re-serialises an IPv4-mapped address in hexadecimal — 'http://[::ffff:127.0.0.1]/' arrives at the guard as '[::ffff:7f00:1]'. The old check matched '::ffff:' followed by a DOTTED quad, a form assertFetchableUrl never receives, so it returned 'not blocked' and the fetch went out. Cloud metadata at [::ffff:169.254.169.254] and RFC1918 at [::ffff:10.0.0.5] went the same way. The existing test asserted the dotted form was blocked and was correct about a string the code never sees — the same shape as every other defect this loop has found: a guard that had only ever been run on input it is not given. Affects crawl-site, check-broken-links, check-security-headers, detect-redirect-chains, analyze-images, check-core-web-vitals and check-mobile-first.

userStories.title: Every edge-function failure told the visitor "[object Object]"
userStories.description: As a visitor whose lead submission is rejected, I need to be told what went wrong and what to do about it, so that a recoverable failure — a mistyped email, a rate limit — does not read as a broken site.
acceptanceCriteria: callEdgeFunction reads the standardized { error: { code, message, details } } shape and throws the message, not the object
The older { error: 'string' } and { message: 'string' } shapes still work
A non-JSON body is only shown when it is short and contains no markup; a proxy's HTML error page falls back to the status line
The HTTP status, the error code and the Retry-After window survive as fields on the thrown error instead of being discarded
A REQUEST_VALIDATION_FAILED response names the fields from error.details, bounded to five
The tests are verified against the shipped implementation: 7 of the 11 fail there
tsc --noEmit clean; no new lint warnings
userStories.notes: Found in iteration 1 of the web-platform loop. _shared/response.ts has answered every failure with error as an OBJECT since it was written, and 23 edge functions import it. The client did errorMessage = errorJson.error || errorJson.message, assigned that object to a string, and threw new Error(object) — whose .message is the literal '[object Object]'. That string is what BuyerInquiryForm, SellerInquiryForm, HomeValuationForm and ContactForm put in their destructive toast, and what Settings, useArticles and the Stripe checkout helpers surfaced too. A rate-limited lead capture said '[object Object]' where submit-lead had sent 'Too many requests. Please try again later.' The code and the Retry-After were discarded with it, so no caller could tell 'slow down' from 'that email is not valid'. Both fixtures in the test are copied from the helpers verbatim, because the bug was that nobody had run the client against what the server actually sends.

src/repo-hygiene.test.ts asserts that path rather than the superseded one
npm run test:run is green on main

The router IS production, so the test was banning the deploy path. userStories.title: One POST to the public lead form took down all 84 edge functions
userStories.description: As the operator of a platform whose entire backend runs in one edge-functions container, I need that container to serve every function the app calls and to survive any single one of them failing, so that a visitor filling in a contact form cannot take the backend offline.
acceptanceCriteria: edge-functions-server.ts discovers functions by reading supabase/functions/ at startup; no literal FUNCTIONS_MAP
A function that registers its handler with top-level serve() is invoked without trying to bind the router's port
Deno.serve is intercepted for the duration of an import and restored afterwards
export default is still honoured, for the 5 functions written against the old router
An unhandled rejection is logged, not fatal
The shim and the import map are copied into the image, and --import-map is passed to both deno cache and deno run
Verified on Deno 1.42.0 (the pinned version) against the image's layout: POST /submit-lead returns the function's own response and /health still answers 200 afterwards
src/edge-function-routing.test.ts fails against the shipped router: 5 of its 8 tests
npm run test:run green, including the repo-hygiene test that was red on main
userStories.notes: Found in iteration 2 while answering US-198. Two defects in the one file that serves production. (1) The router carried a hand-written map of 15 names; the app calls 40, so 29 answered 404 'Function not found' — gdpr-export and gdpr-deletion (GDPR subject access and erasure), create-portal-session/create-stripe-customer/report-stripe-usage (billing), verify-mfa/disable-mfa/login-security/get-sessions/revoke-session (account security), sso-initiate/sso-callback, submit-review, teams, api-keys, send-welcome-email. One mapped name, submit-contact, has no directory. (2) Far worse: it invoked module.default(req), but only 5 of 84 functions export a default and 79 call serve() at module top level. Importing one inside the process that already holds port 8000 raised AddrInUse from an unawaited promise, and an unhandled rejection ends a Deno process. Reproduced on Deno 1.42.0: POST /submit-lead returned 'TypeError: module.default is not a function' as a 500 and then killed the server — /health went from 200 to connection refused. That is an unauthenticated denial of service on the whole backend, reachable from the public lead form, and it would recur on every restart. docs/deploy/edge-functions.md had flagged both as 'worth fixing' and 'verify before building on the current design'; this verified and fixed them.

userStories.title: Columns that do not exist, checked without a database

Five live filter defects fixed: profiles.email in teams (profiles has no email; the address is in auth.users — every invite silently failed to link an existing account), articles.published in analyze-blog-posts-seo (the column is status; the function threw 'No blog posts found to analyze' for every account that had articles), ai_models.model_type in optimize-page-content (no such column; admins who HAD configured a model were told to configure one), seo_alert_rules.user_id in run-scheduled-audit (the table is global and has no user_id; scheduled audits never alerted on anything), seo_performance_budget.page_url in monitor-performance-budget (the column is url_pattern; no configured budget was ever found). Incidentally fixed a pre-existing tsc failure in src/config/og-image.test.ts from @types/node narrowing Buffer.equals.

userStories.title: The SEO and Search Console subsystem writes 59 columns that do not exist
userStories.description: As an operator, I need the SEO and Search Console tooling to actually persist what it computes, so that a feature that appears to run is not discarding every row it writes.
acceptanceCriteria: For each of the 59 entries in KNOWN_BROKEN_WRITES, decide: wrong column name, or missing column
Rename where the column exists under another name (seo_core_web_vitals stores lcp/lcp_pass; the code writes lcp_value/lcp_passed)
Add a migration where the feature genuinely needs a column the table lacks (seo_monitoring_log has 7 columns and the code writes 6 more)
gsc_keyword_performance and gsc_page_performance: the code writes user_id/property_url/keyword/platform; the tables key on property_id and query
Every fixed entry is deleted from KNOWN_BROKEN_WRITES; the stale-entry test enforces this
npm run verify:schema passes against a real Postgres
KNOWN_BROKEN_WRITES is empty and the exception is removed from the test
userStories.notes: ITERATION 4 closed the Google Search Console half: 28 of the 60 references fixed, ratchet down to 32 across 6 tables (articles 4, seo_alerts 5, seo_content_optimization 7, seo_monitoring_log 6, seo_performance_budget 6, seo_semantic_analysis 4). The GSC finding was that the integration was dead end to end: gsc-fetch-properties sent site_url and last_sync_at, neither of which exists, so PostgREST rejected the whole upsert and NO property was ever saved — which is why gsc-sync-data always answered 'No verified GSC property found'. Had it got past that, its own inserts named user_id/property_url/keyword/page_url/platform on tables that key on property_id/query/url. gsc-fetch-core-web-vitals wrote lcp_value/lcp_passed for lcp/lcp_pass across twelve keys; check-core-web-vitals writes the same table correctly and was used as the reference shape. analyze-internal-links sent `url` for a page_url NOT NULL column, so it could not have succeeded even by accident. ITERATION 5 closed the remaining ten tables: 35 more references across 7 functions, leaving only `articles` (4), which genuinely has no SEO-score columns and needs a migration — that is US-202. The headline finding was run-scheduled-audit, broken at four independent levels: its seo_monitoring_log insert sent user_id and check_type (not columns), came back undefined, and the next statement read logEntry.id — so every scheduled audit died with a TypeError seconds after starting; all six audit helpers read schedule.target_urls, which is not a column (it is target_url plus additional_urls), so every loop ran zero times; the alert insert had five wrong keys, a status the CHECK constraint forbids, and no value for a NOT NULL title; and rule.notification_enabled does not exist, so no alert has ever notified anyone. Also fixed: send-seo-notification (an alert stayed 'open' however often it was sent, and a retry re-notified every channel), check-keyword-positions, monitor-performance-budget (six bad keys plus onConflict on a column that does not exist and would not have been unique anyway, plus three of eleven checks measuring against undefined budgets, which `if (check.budget && ...)` counts as passes and which therefore inflated every compliance score), analyze-content, optimize-page-content and analyze-semantic-keywords.

userStories.title: Columns the SEO tables are missing, and the migration they need

The KNOWN_BROKEN_WRITES exception is deleted from src/schema-references.test.ts
userStories.notes: Fixed in iteration 10, once a real Postgres turned out to be available: psql was on PATH and /usr/lib/postgresql/16/bin had the server binaries, so a cluster could be initialised and every migration applied exactly as .github/workflows/verify-backend.yml does. That unblocked the one thing this story was waiting for — regenerating types.ts with npm run types:generate against the applied schema instead of hand-editing a generated file. 20260911000001_seo_analysis_columns.sql adds articles.seo_score / seo_issues / seo_recommendations / last_seo_check (articles already carries seo_title, seo_description and seo_keywords, so SEO metadata lives on the article by convention), seo_core_web_vitals.inp and inp_pass (the table predates INP replacing FID as a Core Web Vital, and US-201 had parked it in field_data), and seo_content_optimization.meta_description / issues / recommendations (it stored page_title but not the description, and had meta_description_suggestions — what to change it TO — with nowhere to record what it IS). userStories.title: The blocking edge-function type-check had never type-checked a function
userStories.description: As a developer, I need the CI gate that claims to type-check all 84 edge functions to actually do it, so that a type error in a payment webhook or a PII backfill fails a build instead of shipping.
acceptanceCriteria: verify-backend.yml excludes supabase/functions/**/*.test.ts from the deno check file list
The list also excludes node_modules, which --node-modules-dir=auto creates under supabase/functions
The job fails loudly if the exclusion ever matches nearly everything
All 14 type errors the gate was hiding are fixed
backfill-lead-pii answers an unauthenticated POST with 401 rather than a router-level 500, verified by running it
deno check over all 103 function files exits 0 on Deno 2.1.4, the major version CI uses
A unit test asserts the exclusion is present and that the vitest specs it excludes still exist
userStories.notes: Found in iteration 6 by RUNNING the functions rather than reading them — the axis CI has never had. The gate globbed `find supabase/functions -name '*.ts'`, which swept up seven vitest specs in _shared/ that `import { describe } from 'vitest'`. Deno cannot resolve a bare specifier, so `deno check` failed module-graph resolution BEFORE type-checking anything, printed one error about an import path, and exited 1. The job's own comment calls it blocking with a cleared 114 -> 0 baseline. Excluding the specs exposed 14 real errors in 3 functions. backfill-lead-pii (7): getCorsHeaders takes an origin, not a Request, and every _shared/response.ts call passed corsHeaders where the Request belongs — including errorResponse('Admin role required', 403, corsHeaders), which puts a number in the code slot. So the function could not return ANY response: each helper called req.headers.get('origin') on a headers bag, threw, and the catch called handleUnexpectedError which threw the same TypeError again. This is the US-086 PII backfill, the prerequisite for the migration that drops the plaintext email and phone columns. trigger-rebuild (1): errorResponse('...', req, 502) with req in the code slot and 502 in the req slot, so the 502 path threw instead of answering. stripe-webhook (6): three helpers typed their client as ReturnType<typeof createClient>, which is the DEFAULT generic instantiation, not what createClient(url, key) infers.

userStories.title: Edge functions answer "you are not logged in" with HTTP 500
userStories.description: As an operator, I need a caller's missing credentials to be reported as 401, so that client errors are not retried like server faults and a real outage is visible against them.
acceptanceCriteria: requireAuth/requireAdmin/requireOwnership throw a typed error carrying 401 or 403 instead of a bare Error
handleUnexpectedError recognises it and answers 401/403, not 500
The body names the cause, so a client can tell 'log in again' from 'the server broke'
Functions that hand-roll a 500 from a caught auth error are fixed too
Re-running the smoke sweep, no function answers an unauthenticated POST with 5xx for an auth reason
A smoke job in CI boots the router and asserts it: deno check cannot see this, and US-199 proves running them finds what type-checking cannot
userStories.notes: Fixed in iteration 7. _shared/http-error.ts adds an HttpError that carries its own status, and requireAuth/requireAdmin/requireOwnership and the two webhook-auth throw sites raise it instead of a bare Error. BOTH error frameworks were taught to recognise it — handleUnexpectedError in _shared/response.ts and handleError in _shared/errors.ts, which google-indexing uses and which had the identical hole. 25 functions hand-roll their own catch block rather than calling either, so `status: 500` in those became `status: errorStatus(error)`, which preserves each function's response envelope (its callers parse it) while fixing the status. send-listing-generator-email threw a bare Error for a missing email, which the same catch turned into a 500; it now throws a 400. Measured, not argued: the same unauthenticated sweep over all 84 functions went from 24 x 401 and 20 x 5xx to 39 x 401 and 5 x 5xx, and the five that remain are honest — three missing a server-side API key, health-check correctly reporting 503 with no database, and google-indexing now 401. scripts/smoke-edge-functions.mjs makes the sweep repeatable (npm run smoke:functions) and it is now a CI job in verify-backend.yml. Run against bef2983 it reports 16 functions and exits 1; against this tree it exits 0. It also asserts the router SURVIVES the sweep, because US-199's crash returned a 500 for the request that caused it and then killed the process — a per-request check alone would have passed. edge-functions-server.ts now honours PORT so the smoke run does not collide with a development router.

userStories.title: 141 browser tests, of which CI ran 6 and let those fail
userStories.description: As a developer, I need every browser suite in this repository to run in CI and to be able to fail, so that a test written to protect something actually protects it.
acceptanceCriteria: ci.yml runs npm run test:e2e in its own job
ci.yml runs npm run test:security in its own job
The accessibility job loses continue-on-error
Both new jobs upload their Playwright report on failure
All three suites were RUN before being wired up, and pass: 22, 113 (+3 skipped), 6
src/browser-suites.test.ts reads the configs, package.json and the workflows, so a fourth suite added without a job fails the unit suite
The guard does not depend on js-yaml, which is only present transitively
userStories.notes: Found in iteration 8 by applying the same 'run it' lens to the frontend. tests/e2e (6 specs, 22 tests: auth, onboarding, public profile visibility, listing deep links, analytics, page builder) and tests/security (4 specs, 113 tests: auth, XSS, security headers, edge-function authz) were committed and no workflow had ever run them. tests/a11y ran, but under continue-on-error: true with the comment 'Warn-only initially', so it could not block a merge. 135 of 141 browser tests were never executed by CI and the other 6 could not fail. All three suites pass as they stand — e2e in 27s, a11y in 16s, security in 5.1 minutes — so nothing had to be fixed, only turned on, which is what makes this the cheap kind of gap and also the easy kind to reintroduce. The suites are hermetic: the e2e config intercepts every /rest/v1, /auth/v1 and /functions/v1 call and supplies the VITE_SUPABASE_* values the client throws without, so no database is involved. Running them locally needed PW_CHROMIUM_PATH, which all three configs already support.

userStories.title: The accessibility baseline was a list of accepted defects
userStories.description: As a visitor with low vision or a screen reader, I need the pages this platform is built to be read on to meet WCAG AA, so that an agent's listings and contact buttons are usable rather than merely present.
acceptanceCriteria: Every BASELINE entry in tests/a11y/accessibility.spec.ts is 0
The one critical violation — an unnamed Radix combobox on the landing page — is fixed with an aria-label and a SelectValue placeholder
Colour contrast reaches 4.5:1 on the landing page, login, register, the dashboard and the public profile, including with the listing modal open
The three duplicated listing status colour maps are replaced by one field on LISTING_STATUSES, which already existed as the single source (US-107)
--muted-foreground clears 4.5:1 against --muted, not only against white
The a11y failure message names the element and its measured ratio, not just a count
6/6 a11y tests pass at baseline 0; the E2E suite still passes; tsc and the unit suite are clean
userStories.notes: Found in iteration 9. US-205 made the a11y job blocking; the baseline it was blocking against was landing 3, login 1, register 1, dashboard 1, public profile 1, modal 1 — eight accepted violations covering roughly 35 elements, with the spec's own comment saying 'Drive these numbers down over time'. What they meant in practice: the blog category filter on the landing page is a Radix SelectTrigger that takes its accessible name from the value it displays, and SelectValue had no placeholder — with no articles loaded there is no matching item, so a screen reader announced 'button', in the empty state every first visitor sees. On the public profile, the listing status badges were white on 500-level fills (Active 2.27:1, Pending 1.9:1) and the bd/ba/sqft unit labels were gray-400 at 2.53:1. In the sticky action bar, Text and Schedule were green-600 and orange-600 — 3.30:1 and 3.56:1 — while Call, Email and Home Value were already fine, because green and orange are the two hues whose 600 step is not dark enough. The footer's legal links were blue-400 in gray-500 prose at 1.9:1 with nothing but colour marking them; they are underlined now. The three copies of the status colour map are gone: LISTING_STATUSES gains a `badge` field, and it also covers off_market, which none of the three maps had — that status rendered an unstyled badge. --muted-foreground moved from 46.9% to 43% lightness because it cleared 4.5:1 on white (4.75) but not on --muted (4.43), the tinted surface it is mostly used against.

userStories.title: The schema checker cannot see a property read on a returned row
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a query that reads a column that does not exist to fail a check, not to read undefined, so that a feature scoring against absent fields is caught the way a bad filter already is.
acceptanceCriteria: Decide whether this is checkable statically: a row from .select('*') is typed `any` in most edge functions, so tsc cannot help
Where a function selects specific columns, the returned row's property reads can be checked against that list
Where it selects '*', check reads against the table's Row type instead
Report the same way src/schema-references.test.ts does, with file and line
Verified against analyze-blog-posts-seo as it was at f21f5b0: four reads reported
userStories.notes: NOTED IN ITERATION 10, NOT FIXED. US-200's checker covers filters, write keys and relation names — the places a column name is a STRING. It cannot see the other half: post.meta_description, post.featured_image, post.published and post.categories in analyze-blog-posts-seo, none of which are columns on `articles` (they are seo_description, featured_image_url, status, and category/tags). The row comes back from .select('*') typed as `any`, so these were undefined rather than errors, and every article analysed was told it was missing a meta description, missing a featured image, unpublished and uncategorised — the score was effectively a constant. Fixed by hand in iteration 10; the class is not guarded. This is harder than the string case and may not be worth a bespoke checker: typing the supabase client with Database in edge functions would let tsc do it, which is the better fix if the deno-check gate can carry it. TESTED IN ITERATION 11 AND RULED OUT: typing the client does not help. With `createClient<Database>(...)` and `import type { Database }` in analyze-blog-posts-seo, deno check still accepted a deliberately misspelled column in an .update() — supabase/functions/deno.json sets strict:false and the rows are `any`, so the generic buys nothing. Extending the regex checker in src/schema-references.test.ts to property reads is the remaining option, and it is harder than the string case because a row's provenance has to be tracked across an alias and a loop.

userStories.title: The a11y suite measured five pages of a thirty-five page site
userStories.description: As a visitor using assistive technology, I need every page of this site to meet WCAG AA, not the five that happen to be in a test list.
acceptanceCriteria: Running axe over every static public route finds zero critical/serious violations
The a11y suite's PAGES list covers every static route App.tsx declares, not a sample
src/browser-suites.test.ts fails when a route is added to App.tsx and not to that list
/admin/* is excluded with its reason stated: the suite's mocks grant no admin role, so visiting them measures a redirect
37 a11y tests pass; the E2E suite still passes; tsc and the unit suite are clean
userStories.notes: Found in iteration 11, one iteration after US-206 drove the baseline to zero — on the five pages the suite looked at. Running axe over all 24 public routes found 14 critical/serious violations on 12 of the 19 it could not see: three more unnamed Radix comboboxes (button-name, CRITICAL) on /blog and the Instagram bio analyzer; 400-level text tokens on light surfaces across every feature and comparison page, down to 1.59:1; and link-in-text-block on the legal pages, where `text-primary hover:underline` gives an in-prose link 1.12:1 against its surroundings and no underline until you hover. Exactly the US-186 shape: the guard was correct and pointed at the wrong pages. The combobox fix on the tools forms is the interesting one — each had a <Label htmlFor="x"> whose id no element carried, because Radix's trigger is a button; giving the trigger that id fixes the dangling htmlFor and names the control at once. Then the route-coverage guard found eight more routes nobody had listed, including TWO free tools (/tools/listing-description-generator, /tools/real-estate-agent-bio-generator) — a whole lead-generation funnel that no browser test had ever loaded. All eight were already clean. 97 colour replacements across 10 pages, 32 links underlined at rest, 7 comboboxes named.

userStories.title: Eight pages the a11y suite reported on but never loaded
userStories.description: As an operator using the admin console daily, I need it held to the same accessibility standard as the marketing pages.
acceptanceCriteria: The a11y suite's mocks can grant an admin session (a user_roles row, and has_role returning true)
/admin, /admin/seo, /admin/audit-log, /admin/health and /admin/search-analytics are measured
The /admin exclusion is removed from the route-coverage test in src/browser-suites.test.ts
Whatever is found is fixed, or recorded with the argument for accepting it
userStories.notes: Fixed in iteration 15, and it turned out to be larger than the admin console. Granting the admin role was the easy half. The hard half: assertAppRendered only checked that SOME text rendered, so a page that redirected still passed — axe reports zero violations on whatever it is given. Adding 'and it must be the page that was asked for' failed EIGHT tests at once: all five admin routes, the onboarding wizard, the SSO callback, and `dashboard`, which has been in this suite since it was written and has been measuring /auth/login the whole time. The cause is that setupMocks intercepts /auth/v1/token and /auth/v1/user, which supabase-js only calls when it has a stored session to refresh — navigating straight to a protected route leaves storage empty, so getSession() returns null without a request and the mock answers nothing. The suite signs in through the form now, the way tests/e2e already did. What the newly-visible pages were hiding: two more CRITICAL button-name violations on the dashboard (the conversion funnel's period filter, and an icon-only copy button), an unnamed progressbar on the dashboard, the onboarding wizard and the admin dashboard — one shadcn component, three pages — and inactive tab triggers at 4.39:1 across the whole application, which is one line in ui/tabs.tsx. 42 a11y tests now, every route App.tsx declares, and the /admin exclusion is gone from src/browser-suites.test.ts.

userStories.title: Both free tools ended at a submit button that did nothing
userStories.description: As an agent trying a free tool, I need the form to tell me what is missing, so that I am not left pressing a button that will never respond.
acceptanceCriteria: Next validates the fields the current step owns and refuses to advance while one is invalid
A refused submit moves the visitor to the step holding the first error, as a backstop
Both tools: a visitor who fills nothing is stopped on the step with the missing field, and sees its message
tests/e2e/free-tool-funnels.spec.ts covers both, and fails against the forms as they were
The E2E suite, the a11y suite, tsc and the unit suite all stay green
userStories.notes: Found in iteration 12 by driving the tools in a browser — US-208 had just discovered that two of them had never been loaded by any test. Both are multi-step react-hook-form forms whose required fields are registered on the early steps, with the submit button on the last. handleSubmit refuses to call the submit handler while any registered field is invalid, and renders each message inside the step that owns the field — which is unmounted by then. Measured before the fix: a visitor filling nothing walked to 'Step 3 of 3' (bio analyzer) and 'Step 4 of 4' (listing generator) with ZERO error messages on the page, and the button there produced no state change, no toast, no console warning and no network request across repeated clicks. These are the lead-generation funnels; the whole purpose of the free tools is capturing an agent's email at the end of one. The bio analyzer requires currentBio (step 1) and city/state/location (step 2) with submit on step 3; the listing generator requires bedrooms/bathrooms/squareFeet/price (step 1) and city/state (step 2) with submit on step 4. Both now validate per step via trigger(), and both send a refused submit back to the offending step.

userStories.title: Every first-time visitor downloaded the whole application twice
userStories.description: As a visitor opening an agent's page from an Instagram bio on a phone, I need to download the application once.
acceptanceCriteria: The service worker reloads only when the visitor accepted the update toast, not on first control
index.html no longer prefetches /auth/login and /auth/register as documents
index.html no longer preconnects to a Supabase host this deployment does not use
Measured on a production build with real cache headers and the service worker ALLOWED: no repeated request on any page
src/lib/register-sw.test.ts fails against the previous behaviour
The E2E, a11y and unit suites all stay green
userStories.notes: Found in iteration 13 by serving dist/ with production cache headers and counting what a browser actually downloads per route — nothing measures that; check-bundle-size.mjs weighs chunks in isolation. Every page fetched its own document, its stylesheet and every entry chunk (index, react-vendor, supabase, state-vendor, ui-vendor) TWICE. Two independent causes. (1) register-sw.ts reloaded on workbox's `controlling` event, which fires when a service worker takes control — including the first registration on a first visit, not only an update. So a first-time visitor loaded the page, registered the worker, and immediately reloaded the whole thing. It now reloads only when the Refresh action on the update toast set updateRequested, which is the one case the reload was written for. (2) index.html carried <link rel="prefetch" as="document"> for /auth/login and /auth/register; they are SPA routes, so each fetched index.html in full. That directly undid US-195, which moved Login and Register out of the entry graph so a public profile would not pay for them, and handed the cost back to every page in a heavier form. Also removed a preconnect to https://supabase.co: this is a self-hosted Supabase at api.agentbio.net, so it was a DNS lookup, TCP connection and TLS handshake to a host the app never contacts. Measured with the service worker allowed: landing 2109 KB / 57 requests -> 1232 KB / 36; public profile 2274 KB / 80 -> 1397 KB / 65; pricing 1913 KB / 49 -> 1035 KB / 28.

userStories.title: Nothing measures what a page costs the visitor who opens it
userStories.description: As a developer, I need a per-route download budget in CI, so that a change which doubles what a visitor fetches fails a build instead of being noticed a year later.
acceptanceCriteria: A script serves dist/ with the same cache headers as public/_headers and loads each key route in Chromium
It asserts a byte and request budget per route, and fails on any URL fetched more than once
The service worker is ALLOWED, because the defect US-211 found only exists on that path
It runs in CI after the build job
Verified against the tree as of 6d5029b, where it fails
userStories.notes: Fixed in iteration 14. scripts/check-route-weight.mjs serves dist/ with the cache policy PARSED FROM public/_headers — not copied — opens each of four routes in Chromium with service workers ALLOWED, and asserts a byte and request budget plus zero repeated URLs. Both choices are load-bearing and both were learned the hard way in iteration 13: a weight measured without `immutable` on hashed assets reported /pricing at 1914 KB when the real figure is 1035, and blocking service workers — the convenient thing to do in a test — hides US-211 entirely, because that reload fired from the worker's `controlling` event. The script refuses to run at all if _headers stops marking assets immutable, rather than printing confident fiction. Verified against the tree at 6d5029b, before US-211: landing 2107 KB / 61 with 23 repeated URLs, pricing 1927 KB / 49 with 19, exit 1. After: 1232 KB / 36 and 1035 KB / 28, nothing fetched twice, exit 0. Runs in the existing Build job, which already has Chromium and a built dist. src/route-weight.test.ts guards the parser and the CI wiring — a matcher that silently stopped matching would put the budget back to measuring the harness.

userStories.title: Anyone with the anon key can delete any account
userStories.description: As an agent, I need my account to be deletable only by me, so that a stranger holding the public anon key cannot erase it.
acceptanceCriteria: New migration: REVOKE EXECUTE ON request_account_deletion, cancel_account_deletion, process_scheduled_account_deletions, request_gdpr_data_export and log_audit_event FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated; GRANT to service_role (or keep authenticated only where the body checks auth.uid() = p_user_id)
request_account_deletion clamps p_grace_period_days to a minimum of 30 and refuses a p_user_id other than auth.uid() for non-service callers

Sweep: ALTER DEFAULT PRIVILEGES IN SCHEMA public REVOKE EXECUTE ON FUNCTIONS FROM anon, authenticated; re-GRANT explicitly every RPC the app calls (derive the list from supabase.rpc( calls in src/ and supabase/functions/)

verify:schema gains a rule: every function executable by anon/authenticated is either on an explicit allowlist or does not take a user id argument; the rule is run against the tree before the fix and fails
verify:schema reproduces the exploit as anon (request with grace -1, then process) and asserts it is now refused
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds, and the existing unit tests still pass
userStories.notes: Found by the 2026-09-30 backend audit and reproduced in a throwaway Postgres: as anon, request_account_deletion(victim,'x',NULL,NULL,-1) followed by process_scheduled_account_deletions() deleted the victim's auth.users row. Baseline contains 0 GRANT/REVOKE statements; Supabase default privileges grant EXECUTE to anon (see scripts/supabase-prelude.sql:124). Do this first. DONE: migration 20260930000001 revokes EXECUTE on all SECURITY DEFINER functions in public from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated (service_role keeps it) and grants back 22: 9 public-by-design (incl. has_role/is_team_* for RLS) and 13 browser RPCs for authenticated. New helpers assert_caller_is(uuid) / assert_caller_is_admin() guard get_user_sessions (was: anyone could read anyone's IPs/locations), get_connected_search_platforms, start_workflow_execution (owner check — US-218 criterion), log_admin_action (was forgeable), get_user_statistics, top_slow_queries, get_system_health_summary. request_account_deletion clamps grace to >=30 days. verify-schema gains three checks: DEFINER_CALLABLE allowlist (84 failures on the pre-fix tree), every src rpc() executable by authenticated (caught get_system_health_summary, which a grep missed), and the exploit reproduced as anon and as another user (9 failures pre-fix incl. 'the victim account was deleted'). Default privileges deliberately NOT altered: a new SECURITY INVOKER RPC should keep working; the allowlist check catches new definer functions instead.

userStories.title: A stranger can rate-limit any agent out of their own leads for ten years
userStories.description: As an agent, I need rate limits that only my own traffic can exhaust, so that nobody can lock me out of pii-crypto, login or my lead form.
acceptanceCriteria: check_rate_limit is no longer executable by anon/authenticated (service_role only)
The rate-limit edge function ignores client-supplied identifier/limitType (or namespaces them under 'client:'), and caps windowSeconds at 3600 — or is deleted if nothing calls it
getClientIP (_shared/validation.ts, _shared/auth.ts) prefers cf-connecting-ip, else the rightmost trusted X-Forwarded-For hop; never the leftmost client-supplied entry
Unit test: a spoofed X-Forwarded-For does not change the resolved IP
verify:schema asserts anon cannot call check_rate_limit
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds, and the existing unit tests still pass
userStories.notes: Reproduced: as anon, check_rate_limit('user:<id>','pii-crypto',1000,315360000) creates a 10-year window. Affects pii-crypto, login-security and submit-lead target buckets. ~20 functions use getClientIP. DONE: check_rate_limit lost anon/authenticated EXECUTE in US-213's deny-by-default migration (enforced by the DEFINER_CALLABLE check). The rate-limit edge function had no caller anywhere and was deleted rather than patched. New _shared/client-ip.ts is the single getClientIP: rightmost X-Forwarded-For entry (TRUSTED_PROXY_HOPS, default 1 = Traefik), cf-connecting-ip only with TRUST_CF_CONNECTING_IP=true — DNS shows functions.agentbio.net resolves straight to the Contabo host, so the old cf-connecting-ip fallback was client-controlled. validation.ts and auth.ts re-export it; four Stripe functions that read the raw header now use it. client-ip.test.ts covers spoofing and asserts no other edge file reads x-forwarded-for. deno check could not run locally (esm.sh/deno.land blocked by the sandbox network policy); client-ip.ts checked standalone, CI runs the full check.

userStories.title: The is_sample flag switches off the whole paywall
userStories.description: As the operator, I need plan limits that the client cannot opt out of, so that a free agent cannot hold 40 links, 30 public listings and unlock every locked lead with one UPDATE.
acceptanceCriteria: A BEFORE INSERT OR UPDATE trigger on every table with is_sample refuses authenticated callers setting or changing is_sample
Sample seeding (src/lib/sample-data-service.ts) moves to a SECURITY DEFINER RPC that only inserts the fixed sample set for auth.uid()
Public read policies on listings (and any other public table with is_sample) add AND NOT is_sample
The links plan-limit trigger fires on UPDATE as well as INSERT
verify:schema reproduces the three bypasses (insert-as-sample-then-flip, public sample listings, UPDATE leads SET is_sample to unlock) and asserts each is refused
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds, and the existing unit tests still pass
userStories.notes: Reproduced by the backend audit. Limit triggers return early on NEW.is_sample (20260923000002:269,290); locked_lead_ids skips samples (20260923000003:242). DONE: migration 20260930000002. guard_is_sample (SECURITY INVOKER so current_user is the caller) on leads/links/listings/testimonials refuses anon/authenticated setting or changing is_sample unless has_role admin; service role passes. Deviation from the criterion: seeding was NOT moved to an RPC — the only writer is the admin SampleDataManager (and sample leads need client-side pii-crypto encryption), so restricting the flag to admins closes the hole with less churn. Public SELECT policies on listings/links/testimonials add AND NOT is_sample. Link and testimonial limit triggers fire on UPDATE OF is_sample too. verify-schema check reproduces the bypasses: 4 failures on the pre-fix tree, passes after. Note: leads has no plaintext email column (US-086) and listings.beds/baths are generated — CLAUDE.md's schema section is stale on both.

userStories.title: A paying agent can stay on the free plan and Stripe will never retry
userStories.description: As a paying agent, I need my payment to change my plan every time, so that I never pay for Professional and get Free.
acceptanceCriteria: stripe-webhook verifies with await stripe.webhooks.constructEventAsync(..., Stripe.createSubtleCryptoProvider()) — the sync constructEvent fails under esm.sh's worker build in Deno
Every database write checks its error and throws; a thrown error returns 500 so Stripe retries
The idempotency claim is released (or marked done only at the end) when processing fails, so a retry is not skipped as duplicate; a missing stripe_processed_events table fails loudly instead of open
A missing user_id in metadata is a 500 with a logged reason, not a silent 200

Handler logic is extracted to a Deno-global-free module and covered by vitest for checkout.session.completed, customer.subscription.updated/deleted and invoice.payment_failed with a mocked client, including a failed-write case that must not return 2xx
Typecheck passes: tsc --noEmit succeeds, and the existing unit tests still pass
userStories.notes: stripe-webhook/index.ts: 19 awaited writes, 3 error checks; claimEvent at :52-72 records before work; constructEvent at :224. Related history: US-118, US-146 (stripe_processed_events missing in production). DONE: logic moved to stripe-webhook/handler.ts (no Deno globals, type-only esm.sh imports) with 19 vitest cases over a fake client. index.ts verifies with constructEventAsync + createSubtleCryptoProvider; a bad signature is the only 400. Every entitlement write goes through must() and throws; a failure releases the stripe_processed_events claim and answers 500 so Stripe's retry runs. A plan-lookup DB error now throws instead of recording 'free'. Missing metadata.user_id falls back to stripe_customers by customer id, else 500. userStories.notes: oauth-proxy/index.ts:45-49 state=btoa(JSON) incl verifier, :107 parse w/o signature, :149 logs tokenData, :156 atob no email_verified, :164-165 listUsers() unpaged, :167-185 createUser then error. sso-callback/index.ts:202-203 same listUsers bug (known follow-up). Secret name: reference an env var (e.g. OAUTH_STATE_SECRET), list it as an owner action. DONE: Verified every audit claim in the notes against the code and found all of them accurate (oauth-proxy:45-49, :107, :149, :156, :164-185; sso-callback:202-203). (1) New migration 20261101000011_auth_user_id_by_email.sql adds public.auth_user_id_by_email(p_email text) returns uuid. It is SECURITY DEFINER and STABLE, pins search_path = public, extensions, pg_temp, matches lower(email) and skips soft-deleted users, is REVOKEd from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated and GRANTed to service_role. The new module _shared/auth-user-lookup.ts (findAuthUserIdByEmail, isEmailExistsError) is used by both oauth-proxy and sso-callback. A failed lookup throws rather than being read as 'no account'. If createUser returns email_exists because a concurrent sign-in created the account first, oauth-proxy treats it as an existing user. (2) New module oauth-proxy/oauth.ts. State is '<base64url JSON {p,r,n,exp}>.<HMAC-SHA256>' with a 600 s expiry. The PKCE verifier is HMAC(secret, 'pkce:'+nonce), derived again at callback, and never appears in the state. A tampered, foreign-key, expired, malformed or old btoa-style state gets a 400. checkSocialIdToken decodes the token as base64url (reusing sso.ts decodeJwtPayload), checks iss, aud and exp, and refuses any email that is not verified. The user is sent to /auth/login?error=email_not_verified. tokenErrorForLog logs only the `error` field, which covers the oauth-proxy:149 PII log line US-259 also targets. redirect_to is now limited to a same-site path (safeRedirectPath blocks //host, backslashes, absolute URLs and control characters). Unsupported providers are refused before any redirect. (3) types.ts was regenerated, adding one line for auth_user_id_by_email. OAUTH_STATE_SECRET was added to supabase/functions/.env.example (the env-example test requires it). Test-first: oauth.test.ts has 20 tests. Its 'callers' tests (no listUsers in either function; no tokenData log and no atob in oauth-proxy) failed against the old index.ts, and all pass after the change. DEVIATIONS: (a) The criterion says email_verified !== true is refused. Apple has historically sent email_verified as the string "true", so both the boolean true and the string "true" are accepted. Everything else is refused, including false, "false", a missing claim and non-boolean values. (b) The signing secret falls back to an HMAC key derived from SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY ('oauth-state-v1:'+key) when OAUTH_STATE_SECRET is unset or shorter than 32 characters, so sign-in does not break before the owner sets the secret. If neither is set, the function returns 503 instead of running unsigned. (c) The state is not tied to the browser by a cookie, so login-CSRF hardening is a possible follow-up. Apple still has no PKCE, as before. (d) Sign-ins that started before the deploy and are still in progress will get a 400 'Invalid state' once and need to retry. (e) There is no deno binary in the sandbox. Instead, oauth-proxy/index.ts and sso-callback/index.ts were type-checked with strict tsc plus a small shim for the https imports, and the only error was a pre-existing unused import in _shared/auth.ts.

userStories.notes: main.tsx:8,17 static initSentry; sentry.ts:8 import * as Sentry, :96 replayIntegration; errorHandler.ts:5, ErrorBoundary.tsx:3, RouteErrorBoundary.tsx:3 static imports. Measured entry 64,942 B no DSN vs 145,864 B with DSN. DONE: Verified the audit notes first and they were all correct: main.tsx:8,17 calls initSentry statically, sentry.ts:8 is `import * as Sentry`, sentry.ts:96 is replayIntegration, and errorHandler.ts, ErrorBoundary.tsx and RouteErrorBoundary.tsx import the facade statically. Baseline entry was 65,053 B gzip with no DSN and 145,889 B with a DSN. src/lib/sentry.ts is now a facade with no @sentry import; initSentry() adds early error/unhandledrejection listeners and loads the SDK (sentry-sdk.ts) via dynamic import at requestIdleCallback after load, then Session Replay (sentry-replay.ts) from its own chunk via addIntegration. Calls before load go into a 50-event capped buffer (overflow recorded as a breadcrumb); user/tags/context keep latest values; captureException/captureMessage return a pre-generated event id that matches the Sentry event. Without a DSN (or outside production without VITE_SENTRY_ENABLED=true) everything is a no-op and the SDK is never fetched. vite.config.ts adds sentry-vendor and sentry-replay-vendor chunks; scripts/check-bundle-size.mjs fails if Sentry code is in the first-paint graph (and, with a DSN set, if no chunk contains the SDK); BUNDLE_DIST points it at another dir; CI's bundle-size job builds with a dummy DSN. With a DSN the entry is now 62,806 B gzip (+978 B over no DSN). src/lib/sentry.test.ts adds 9 tests (all failed on the old code). DEVIATIONS: Removed unused exports SentryErrorBoundary, SentryProfiler, startTransaction and `export { Sentry }` (keeping them required a static SDK import); Breadcrumb/SeverityLevel types are now local. Full `npm run build` with prerender was not run with a DSN (no Playwright Chromium in sandbox); CI is the first place prerender runs with the lazy SDK. Integrator re-ran vite build with a DSN on the merged tree: check-bundle-size reports 'Sentry SDK is lazy' and passes.

userStories.title: Agents could not see which of their listings visitors open
userStories.description: Since US-227 the public profile has saved a 'listing_view' event each time a visitor opens a listing, but nothing ever read those events back. Agents had no per-listing view counts anywhere, while Landing and /features/analytics promise "see which listings visitors view most". This is the per-listing views slice of US-141 (the second acceptance criterion's dashboard half).
acceptanceCriteria: listing_view_stats() returns one row per listing that the caller (auth.uid()) owns and visitors opened. Each row has views_7d, views_30d, visitors_30d and last_viewed_at, all inside the plan analytics window (analytics_visible_since).
Events whose target_id points at another agent's listing (visitors can insert any target_id) are not counted. Events older than 30 days and non-listing_view events are not counted either.
listing_view_stats is SECURITY INVOKER with search_path pinned. EXECUTE is revoked from PUBLIC and anon and granted to authenticated and service_role.
Dashboard Listings grid cards show '<N> views · <M> this week', or 'No views in 30 days'. A screen reader and the title attribute get the full description with the visitor count.
The list view gains a 'Views (30d)' column.
While the counts are loading or after the query fails, no views line or column is shown, so a card never shows 'No views' it did not count.
Unit tests cover the row parser and the wording, component tests cover the card and the column, and a verify:schema check covers scoping, the windows and the anon refusal.
userStories.notes:
**What was wrong (evidence):**
- trackListingView fires listing_view on every listing open: src/lib/analyticsEvents.ts:150-153, called from src/pages/public/FullProfilePage.tsx:108.
- The CHECK constraint accepts that event type: supabase/migrations/20260930000007_funnel_events_and_campaign_conversion.sql:15-20.
- analytics_summary() keeps a label only for link_click (supabase/migrations/20261028000007_analytics_summary.sql:80), so all listing views fall into one unlabelled count.
- No dashboard file read listing_view.
- The broken promises: src/pages/public/Landing.tsx:461 and src/pages/features/Analytics.tsx:157.

**What changed:**
- **New migration** `supabase/migrations/20261107000263_listing_view_stats.sql`:
  - a partial index on analytics_events (user_id, target_id, occurred_at DESC) WHERE event_type='listing_view';
  - `listing_view_stats()`: SECURITY INVOKER, search_path pinned, no user id argument. It joins listings on target_id with l.user_id = auth.uid(), so a forged target id is dropped. The window is greatest(now()-30d, analytics_visible_since()). EXECUTE is revoked from PUBLIC/anon and granted to authenticated/service_role.
  - The filename ends in 000263 (the story id) so it cannot clash with other lanes' migrations from the same day.
- **types.ts:** a hand-added listing_view_stats entry, in the same shape the generator emits for TABLE returns (`Record<string, unknown>[]`).
- **New `src/lib/listingViews.ts`:** toListingViewStats (a tolerant row parser), formatListingViews and describeListingViews.
- **New `src/hooks/useListingViewStats.ts`:** a TanStack query with 5-minute staleTime. It exposes `isReady`, which stays false while loading and after an error.
- **`src/pages/dashboard/Listings.tsx`:** the grid card footer gets an Eye icon and the views line. The full description is in sr-only text and the title attribute; the short line is aria-hidden. The list view gets a 'Views (30d)' column, hidden below md.
- **`scripts/verify-schema.mjs`:** a new check, 'listing_view_stats counts views per own listing, and nothing else'. It seeds 3 events in the last 7 days, 2 at 20 days, 1 at 45 days, a forged event on another agent's listing, the other agent's own event and a link_click. It expects exactly one row with 3 / 5 / 5, and expects anon to be refused.

I did not edit prd.json or progress.txt, and I did not push. The lint-staged pre-commit hook reformatted listingViews.test.ts with prettier (formatting only).

userStories.title: The public profile page waited for its own code to download before it asked for any data
userStories.description: /:slug (the agent page in every Instagram bio) rendered the lazy FullProfilePage directly. The steps ran strictly one after another: entry JS, then the FullProfilePage chunk and its imports, then mount, then the profiles row, then six related reads. The Supabase round trips could not start until the code that sends them had arrived. Now a small ProfileRoute component, in the entry chunk, starts the same query as soon as the route matches. The chunk download and the data reads now run at the same time, and the page's useQuery picks up the request already in flight instead of sending a second one.
acceptanceCriteria: The profile read for /:slug starts before the FullProfilePage chunk resolves (test: a lazy chunk that never resolves still produces the profiles read with username canonicalised, followed by the listings/testimonials/links/user_settings reads)
When the page mounts, its usePublicProfile reuses the query already started: exactly one profiles read
The route-level fallback is the page's own ProfileSkeleton, not the generic 'Loading page...' spinner, so the visitor sees one continuous skeleton
An empty slug sends no read
check-bundle-size passes: the entry graph still has none of the forbidden chunks, and the entry chunk grows by 1.25 KB gzip at most
userStories.notes:
Audit: the open performance story US-125 is mostly done already. Source maps were handled in US-160 and jspdf in US-162, and check-bundle-size currently passes: 246 chunks, one documented exception (three-vendor). What is left of US-125 is matching Radix by prefix and an eslint ratchet. Neither has real user impact, so I chose a change to the critical path of the most-visited page instead.

Evidence of the waterfall:
- src/App.tsx:337 had `<Route path="/:slug" element={<ProfilePage />} />` with ProfilePage = lazy(FullProfilePage) (App.tsx:140).
- The only data request was usePublicProfile at src/pages/public/FullProfilePage.tsx:84, inside that lazy chunk.
- usePublicProfile (src/hooks/usePublicProfile.ts) reads the profiles row first, then six reads in parallel with Promise.all.
- So the data could only start after the chunk arrived (FullProfilePage-*.js is 85 KB and loads about 50 more chunks) and the component had mounted.

Change:
- src/hooks/usePublicProfile.ts: the query is now `publicProfileQueryOptions(rawUsername)`, built with TanStack's queryOptions and using the same key ['public-profile', username]. usePublicProfile is a thin useQuery wrapper over it, so behaviour and callers are unchanged.
- New file src/components/profile/ProfileRoute.tsx: it reads the slug, calls queryClient.prefetchQuery from an effect, and renders the lazy page inside its own Suspense with a ProfileSkeleton fallback. The Suspense boundary has to sit below the effect. Otherwise the component never commits, and the prefetch would not run until the chunk arrived.
- src/App.tsx: the route is now `<ProfileRoute page={ProfilePage} />`.
- New test file src/components/profile/ProfileRoute.test.tsx (4 tests). I checked that the prefetch test and the no-duplicate test both fail with the prefetch commented out.

Measured with vite build, before and after (minified, gzip in brackets):
- Entry index chunk: 210.42 KB (60.32) before, 214.28 KB (61.57) after.
- FullProfilePage chunk: 85.51 KB (24.13) before, 81.90 KB (23.15) after.
- Bytes for a profile visitor are about the same: +1.25 KB gzip on the entry, -0.98 KB gzip on the profile chunk.
- The gain is latency. The two Supabase round trips (profiles, then six in parallel) now overlap the profile chunk download instead of following it. I did not measure LCP in a browser because Playwright's browser is not installed in this sandbox, so check-route-weight could not run. Expect the saving to be the smaller of the chunk-graph load time and the two round trips, typically a few hundred ms on mobile.

One known edge case: for a username that does not exist, if the prefetch fails before the chunk mounts, react-query's retryOnMount sends the read once more. That is the 404 path only, and it does no harm.

lint-staged ran a git stash backup during the commit and cleaned it up; `git stash list` is empty afterwards.

userStories.title: Agents' URLs went into links and page navigation without a real scheme check, and the CSP allowed scripts from esm.sh
userStories.description: The old sanitizeUrl (src/utils/sanitize.ts:115-141) checked a trimmed, lowercased copy with startsWith('javascript:') and handed back anything it didn't recognise unchanged. The WHATWG URL parser strips tabs and newlines inside a scheme and C0 control characters around it, so "java\tscript:alert(1)" and "\u0001javascript:alert(1)" both got through. Verified in Node: new URL('java\tscript:alert(1)') resolves to javascript:alert(1). The result is assigned to window.location.href by LinkBlock.tsx:27 and CTABlock.tsx:24, which render on the public /:username page through CustomBlocksSection. The public profile also put links.url (CustomLinks.tsx:115), the social profile URLs (SocialLinks.tsx:79) and listings.virtual_tour_url (ListingDetailModal.tsx:461) into href with no check at all. Separately, script-src in both public/_headers and the index.html meta CSP listed https://esm.sh, which nothing in the frontend loads and which serves any npm package as a script.
acceptanceCriteria: sanitizeUrl strips characters the way the URL parser does, then parses the value, and allows only http:, https:, mailto: and tel:, plus same-site paths that start with a single /
Protocol-relative //host and /\host are refused; a bare host such as zillow.com/me gets https:// added instead of becoming a relative agentbio.net link
sanitizeExternalUrl allows http(s) only, and is used for social URLs and virtual tours
The public CustomLinks, SocialLinks and ListingDetailModal leave out entries whose URL is unsafe instead of rendering them as an href
The Add and Edit link forms refuse a URL the public page would drop, and save the cleaned-up value
esm.sh is removed from script-src in public/_headers and index.html, and a test fails if a package CDN, 'unsafe-inline', 'unsafe-eval', *, https: or data: is added back
tsc passes and the full vitest suite passes
userStories.notes:
What changed:

userStories.description: gdpr-export (the "Download my data" button, src/hooks/useGDPR.ts:64) now reads every section in full. It pages past PostgREST's 1,000-row cap, ordered by id. If any query fails, it returns a 503 that names the failed sections, where before it handed out a file that looked complete but had empty sections. userStories.notes:
I picked this from the "Not included" list in progress.txt:4858-4859 ("GDPR export swallowing query errors (and missing lead_activities)"). prd.json has no open story tagged lane=enterprise. US-085 (native MFA) and US-133 are open but too large for one session.

What was wrong, in the old supabase/functions/gdpr-export/index.ts:
- Seventeen queries, none checking `error`. Each result was coalesced with `|| []`, so a failed query exported as "no data", and the request was still marked completed.
- Every list was a single request, so the 1,000-row cap truncated it silently. Hand-set limits cut further: analytics_views 1000, login_attempts 100, audit_logs 500.
- Lead activity, custom pages, workflows, notifications, subscriptions, invoices, team memberships, roles, API keys and analytics events were never exported.
- gdpr_data_requests was read with select('*'), so the subject was handed the verification_token_hash.
- The pending request was closed with an update().order().limit() chain, and its error was ignored.
- p_details was sent as a JSON string, not an object.

What changed:
- New supabase/functions/gdpr-export/collect.ts, with no Deno globals:
  - a SECTIONS spec list;
  - readAllRows, which pages by id with range() until it gets a short page;
  - a per-section ceiling of 100,000 rows, reported in meta.truncated;
  - collectSections, which reads sections in parallel and throws ExportIncompleteError listing the failed sections in a fixed order;
  - helpers sectionCounts and maskLoginAttempt.
- index.ts now:
  - adapts the service-role client to ExportReader (page uses .range, single sections use .maybeSingle, so a missing row is null rather than an error);
  - on failure returns 503 with failedSections, writes a failure audit entry and calls reportError;
  - builds the export document, keeping the old top-level keys and adding billing, teams, analytics.events, security.apiKeys and meta (counts and truncated);
  - closes the pending request by finding it by id first, and logs any error;
  - writes a success audit entry with per-section counts.
- Rate limit raised from 1 to 3 exports per hour. An attempt is counted before the export runs, so with 1, a transient 503 would lock the user out for an hour.

Existing UI needs no change: callEdgeFunction (src/lib/edgeFunctions.ts:98) already shows the JSON error message in the toast.

userStories.title: The installed app never got a new offline shell, kept every old code chunk on the phone forever, and kept running an old copy of the cookie-consent script
userStories.description: The PWA service worker now gets a new version stamp on every build, so each deploy installs a fresh worker and offline shell. Its runtime and image caches have a size cap and are trimmed. Scripts whose file names carry no content hash (/scripts/analytics.js, which holds the GA consent check) are fetched from the network first instead of being served from cache forever, and _headers now makes browsers revalidate /scripts/* instead of caching it as immutable for a year. Also, the Retry button on the offline page did nothing because the CSP blocks its inline onclick. It is now a plain form.
acceptanceCriteria: dist/sw.js carries a build-specific VERSION (verified: const VERSION = '78c8206be01b' after vite build); public/sw.js ships the single placeholder const VERSION = 'dev'
A new version installs a new precache and deletes the old one; the runtime and image caches carry over between versions
agentbio-sw-runtime-v1 is capped at 150 entries and agentbio-sw-images-v1 at 80, oldest first; caches left oversized by the old worker are trimmed on activate
Only /assets/* (hashed) is CacheFirst; same-origin .js/.mjs/.css outside /assets is NetworkFirst with a cached fallback for offline; fonts are StaleWhileRevalidate
_headers /scripts/* comes after /*.js and sets max-age=0, must-revalidate (no immutable)
Auth, Supabase, requests with an Authorization header, and non-GET requests are still never cached (tested)
offline.html Retry works under the CSP (a GET form, no inline handler)
userStories.notes:
Evidence before the change: public/sw.js had VERSION = 'v1' hard-coded and public/ is copied verbatim, so the file was the same on every deploy. The browser therefore never installed a new worker, and the APP_SHELL precache ('/', '/index.html') stayed whatever a visitor got on first install. The offline fallback (networkFirstNavigation -> caches.match('/index.html')) then served a homepage that pointed at deleted chunks. isStaticAsset matched any .js/.css, so /scripts/analytics.js (the cookie-consent gate on GA, see src/lib/cookie-consent.ts) was CacheFirst for good. Cache puts were never trimmed and never awaited. In _headers, /*.js was set to max-age=31536000, immutable, which also covered /scripts/analytics.js. progress.txt:4861-4862 lists both problems under "Not included".

Changes:
- public/sw.js: added a VERSION placeholder. Only PRECACHE is versioned; RUNTIME and IMAGES keep their US-027 names, so existing caches are adopted and trimmed, and tabs opened before a deploy can still load their old chunks after Cloudflare drops them. Added MAX_ENTRIES and trimCache (FIFO via cache.keys() insertion order), a store() helper run inside event.waitUntil, a trim on activate, and new routing (isHashedAsset / isFont / isUnhashedCode).
- src/config/sw-version.ts (new): buildIdFromFileNames (sha of the sorted emitted file names, 12 hex characters, deterministic) and stampServiceWorkerVersion. The stamp throws unless the placeholder appears exactly once, and only accepts ids made of [A-Za-z0-9_-].
- vite.config.ts: a 'sw-build-version' plugin (apply: build, writeBundle) that rewrites <outDir>/sw.js.
- public/_headers: a /scripts/* rule placed after /*.js.
- public/offline.html: the Retry button is now a form.

How verified: src/sw.test.ts runs the real public/sw.js in a node:vm context against a fake Cache Storage and a fake fetch. A real vite build to scratchpad confirmed the stamp in dist/sw.js. lint-staged's prettier and eslint reformatted at commit time; I re-ran tsc and the tests after that and both passed.

VERIFIED: npx tsc --noEmit: passed, no output (re-run after the lint-staged reformat: TSC_OK).
npx vitest run src/sw.test.ts: 11/11 passed.
npx vitest run src/sw.test.ts src/deployed-files.test.ts src/route-weight.test.ts src/lib: 56 files, 575 tests passed.
After the commit-time format: npx vitest run src/sw.test.ts src/deployed-files.test.ts: 22/22 passed.
npx vite build --outDir <scratchpad>/dist: exit 0, dist/sw.js line 31 reads const VERSION = '78c8206be01b'.
npx tsc -p tsconfig.node.json: TS6307 for src/config/sw-version.ts. homepage-seo.ts gets the same error, so this was already true before my change, and CI does not run this check.
No migration, so verify:migrations was not run.

REVIEW: fix_required; fix-up: The reviewer was right. In public/sw.js, `networkFirst` called `fetch(request)` with the default cache mode. That strategy is only used for unhashed code, which today means /scripts/analytics.js. The browser HTTP cache answers that kind of fetch, so anyone who loaded analytics.js under the old `/*.js` header (`max-age=31536000, immutable`) would keep getting the old copy. The fix did not reach them.

Fix: `networkFirst` now calls `fetch(request, { cache: 'no-cache' })`. This makes the browser check with the server before using its stored copy, so the deployed consent gate reaches existing visitors. When offline, the worker still falls back to its own cached copy. I extended the comment above `isUnhashedCode`, because the old one wasn't true for those visitors. It now explains why the request uses 'no-cache'.

Test: in src/sw.test.ts, the fake `fetch` now records the options it is called with. A new test checks that the /scripts/analytics.js request uses `cache: 'no-cache'`.

Committed as f60d817 "US-272: address review" with the requested trailers. `loop/r1-mobile` now points at f60d817. Not pushed; prd.json and progress.txt were not touched.

Evidence of the bug:
- The visitor policies were last recreated in supabase/migrations/20260930000002_is_sample_is_not_client_writable.sql:60-74. They checked only status, is_active or is_published on the row itself, plus is_sample. They never looked at profiles.is_published, and had no TO clause, so they applied to PUBLIC.
- The open-house functions (20260923000001_client_sphere_and_open_houses.sql:302 and :350) used `is_published IS NOT FALSE`, which lets NULL through. The profile row policy (20260808000002:145) treats NULL as unpublished.
- public_agent_response_hours (20260902000010:31) answered for any user id.

The fix is in supabase/migrations/20261107000308_unpublished_agent_content_private.sql:
- The three visitor policies now also require `EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM public.profiles p WHERE p.id = <table>.user_id AND p.is_published IS TRUE)`, and are scoped TO anon, authenticated. This check runs with the caller's own rights. It only needs what anon and authenticated can already read: published profile rows, plus the id and is_published columns. So no new SECURITY DEFINER function was needed.
- The owner keeps access through the existing own-row policies, which are ORed with these.
- The open-house functions now use `(p.is_published IS TRUE OR o.user_id = auth.uid())`. Their bodies and return types are otherwise unchanged, and grants are restated.
- public_agent_response_hours gets the same check, and returns NULL otherwise.
- The migration can be re-run safely (DROP IF EXISTS / CREATE OR REPLACE).

- usePublicProfile already filters on is_active and is_published on the client.
- functions/[username].ts reads listings with the anon key, so it now respects unpublishing too, which is what we want.
- submit-lead uses the service role and is not affected.

userStories.title: Overdue-lead chaser stopped chasing once 500 old leads piled up, re-sent reminders hourly, and ignored the 1-hour SLA
userStories.description: Picks up open slice US-292. The hourly overdue-lead chaser in scheduled-maintenance now reads every unanswered lead from 1 hour to 7 days old, in pages. It chases each lead at most once, with a unique index backing that up. A failed read now fails the task instead of sending the reminder again. Each agent gets one email per run instead of one per lead. A missed run is made up by the next one, as long as the lead is inside the 7-day window.
acceptanceCriteria: A lead is chased at most once, across any number of runs and when two runs overlap: the notification insert is the claim, and a second claim (23505 on idx_notifications_lead_overdue_once) is treated as already chased and not emailed
If the already-chased read fails, the task fails; it does not send again
The window covers leads created between 7 days and 1 hour ago, so a missed run is made up by the next run, and leads older than 7 days are never chased (no flood on first deploy)
A backlog of chased-but-unanswered leads cannot starve new ones: the whole window is read in pages of 1,000, up to 10,000 rows, and the summary says if that ceiling is hit
An agent on a 1-hour SLA is chased after 1 hour; an sla_hours value Settings does not offer falls back to 2
One email per agent per run lists all leads claimed in that run (10 named, then 'and N more')
An agent whose profile cannot be read is left unclaimed and retried next run, and the task reports failed (207)
userStories.notes:
Setup: this worktree started at main (80eb63c), which is behind the loop branch. I hard-reset it to claude/continuous-improvement-loops-fx2ob1 (21c8b0d) before starting, so it holds US-263..US-302 and the round-1 work. node_modules is symlinked to the main checkout.

What was wrong, in the old supabase/functions/scheduled-maintenance/index.ts (before this commit):
- Lines 85-91: `.eq('status','new').is('first_responded_at',null).lt('created_at',cutoff).order('created_at',asc).limit(500)`. A lead nobody answers stays `new` forever, so once 500 of them existed across all agents, every run re-read the same already-chased backlog and no newer lead was ever chased again. There was also no lower bound, so the first run, or an agent turning chasing back on, emailed about leads that were months old.
- Line 82: the net was cast at DEFAULT_SLA_HOURS = 2, but Settings offers [1,2,4,8,24] (src/components/settings/LeadNotificationPreferences.tsx:26). An agent on 1 hour was chased an hour late. The comment there claimed it used the shortest window.
- Lines 128-134: the dedupe read ignored its `error` and used `.maybeSingle()`, which errors when it finds two rows. Either way `already` came back null and the lead was chased again, every hour, adding more duplicates each time. There was also a race between that check and the insert.
- Lines 156-165: one email per lead. sla_hours was used unvalidated.

What changed:
- New file supabase/functions/scheduled-maintenance/overdue.ts, with no Deno globals:
  - an OverdueStore interface;
  - chaseOverdueLeads, which pages the window, loads the chased set in bulk per 200 agents (a failed read throws), claims each lead by inserting its notification, and sends one email per agent for the leads it claimed;
  - helpers slaHoursFor, candidateWindow, buildChaseEmail and summarizeOverdueReport.
- index.ts:
  - adds an overdueStore() adapter over the service-role client: candidates are ordered by created_at then id and read with range(); the notifications read is paged; claim maps error 23505 to 'duplicate';
  - the overdue_leads task throws when report.errors is non-empty, matching how the account_deletions task reports failure;
  - the inline chaser and its constants are gone.
- New migration supabase/migrations/20261107000309_lead_overdue_once.sql:
  - deletes duplicate lead_overdue notifications, keeping the earliest per (user_id, data->>'lead_id');
  - creates the unique partial index idx_notifications_lead_overdue_once ON notifications (user_id, (data->>'lead_id')) WHERE type='lead_overdue'.
  - No function, policy or grant changes.
- Until the migration is applied the code still works: the bulk pre-check does the deduping, and the index only closes the race between overlapping runs.

Tested against a real Postgres 16 (a throwaway cluster, since deleted):
- the DELETE removed the later duplicate and left non-lead_overdue rows alone;
- the index was built;
- a duplicate insert raised a unique violation on idx_notifications_lead_overdue_once.

userStories.title: The installed app opened offline to the homepage, or a blank screen after a deploy, instead of the route the agent had already visited
userStories.description: US-300 slice, done as US-312. The service worker in public/sw.js now saves the HTML of every same-origin page that loads successfully. It goes in a capped cache, agentbio-sw-pages-v1, keyed by path. When offline, a page is served in this order: the copy saved for that exact path, then the precached /index.html, then /offline.html, then a 503. Separately, src/lib/sw-cleanup.ts now logs through logger instead of console.
acceptanceCriteria: Successful same-origin navigations are saved in agentbio-sw-pages-v1, capped at 30 entries with the oldest dropped first (tested)
