Redirected, non-200, non-HTML and Cache-Control no-store responses are never saved. Navigations under /auth go straight to the network and are never saved (tested)
The cache key is origin + path with the query string dropped, so utm/ref/session_id variants share one entry (tested)
The pages cache survives a new worker version and is trimmed on activate (tested)
sw-cleanup.ts has no console calls; everything goes through logger (tested)
userStories.notes:
Setup: the worktree started at 80eb63c, which is older than round 1. Before working I fast-forwarded it to claude/continuous-improvement-loops-fx2ob1 (21c8b0d), the same base the other round-2 lanes use. US-300 and US-301 were only in /home/user/plain-page-link/prd.json, not in the stale worktree copy.

Why it matters: before this change, networkFirstNavigation in public/sw.js answered every offline navigation with caches.match(request) or '/index.html'. The worker only precaches APP_SHELL ('/', '/index.html', '/offline.html', '/manifest.json'), not the JS files that page loads. So after any deploy, the precached /index.html points at a new entry file the phone has never downloaded, and opening the installed app offline gave a blank screen. A page's own saved HTML points at the JS files that loaded with it, and those sit in agentbio-sw-runtime-v1 (US-272).

The note on US-300 asked me to check main.tsx: it mounts with ReactDOM.createRoot(...).render (src/main.tsx, around line 76) and never calls hydrateRoot. So serving one route's saved HTML is safe, because React renders whatever URL it is on.

Changes:
- /home/user/plain-page-link/.claude/worktrees/wf_00174b25-d3a-10/public/sw.js:
  - Adds the PAGES cache with a cap of 30 in MAX_ENTRIES.
  - New pageKey() builds the key from origin + path.
  - New isCacheablePage() saves only a 200 HTML response that was not redirected, is basic or default, and is not marked no-store.
  - networkFirstNavigation(event, request, url) saves pages through event.waitUntil(store(...)) and uses the new offline order.
  - activate keeps PAGES and trims it. It is unversioned, like RUNTIME and IMAGES.
- /home/user/plain-page-link/.claude/worktrees/wf_00174b25-d3a-10/src/sw.test.ts: 9 new tests in 'offline pages for visited routes (US-312)'. The request() helper now strips mode and destination before calling new Request, because Node rejects mode 'navigate'.
- /home/user/plain-page-link/.claude/worktrees/wf_00174b25-d3a-10/src/lib/sw-cleanup.ts: console.log/error replaced with logger.debug/info/error, with the URL passed as context.

  - The app worker and its agentbio-sw-* caches, including pages-v1, are kept; the legacy firebase worker and the workbox cache are removed.

Two templates had link buttons pointing at '#': First-Time Buyer had "First-Time Buyer Guide (Free Download)" and Investor had "Market Analysis Report". The Luxury and Simple Clean contact forms promised a reply "within 24 hours", and the Investor form promised "I'll prepare a custom market analysis for you". If an agent applied a template without editing it, all of this went live on /:username. The template copy is fixed. On top of that, a link with no real destination ('', '#', an unsafe scheme, or an example.com/.org/.net host) no longer appears on the public page. Pages already saved from the old templates live as jsonb rows, so this hides their dead buttons too, with no migration needed.
acceptanceCriteria: No template link, hero or CTA URL lacks a real destination (usableLinkUrl is non-empty for each)
No template link button title mentions a download, guide, report or 'free'
No template contact form's successMessage commits the agent to a response time, and every form has one
A link block whose URL is '', '#', an example.* host or an unsafe scheme renders nothing on the public page, and CustomBlocksSection drops it
In the editor, such a block shows a note saying it is hidden on the public page until it has a URL
A new Link block defaults to an empty URL, not https://example.com

Evidence before the fix: src/lib/pageTemplates.ts ~163-171 had a First-Time Buyer link with title '📚 First-Time Buyer Guide (Free Download)' and url '#'. ~276-284 had the Investor link '📊 Market Analysis Report' with url '#'. Line 109 (Luxury) and line 584 (Simple Clean) had "within 24 hours". The Investor form said "I'll prepare a custom market analysis for you." src/lib/pageBuilder.ts:273 defaulted a new Link block to https://example.com. LinkBlock sent visitors wherever sanitizeUrl pointed, and '#' passed through it unchanged.

Changes:

- src/components/pageBuilder/blocks/LinkBlock.tsx returns null on the public page when there is no usable URL. In the editor it shows a role=note hint.
- src/components/profile/CustomBlocksSection.tsx filters these blocks out so they leave no empty gap in the flex column.
- src/lib/pageTemplates.ts: the First-Time Buyer button is now 'Ask me anything about buying your first home', pointing at '#contact'. FullProfilePage.tsx:608 has section id="contact", so the link goes somewhere. The Investor link block is removed, since its contact form follows directly. All success messages now say "soon" and make no time commitment.
- src/lib/pageBuilder.ts: the Link block's default URL is ''.
- src/components/pageBuilder/BlockSettings.tsx: realistic placeholder text and a hint line under the URL field.
- src/components/pageBuilder/blocks/ContactBlock.tsx: the success panel falls back to a sentence when successMessage is empty. Before, it showed an empty paragraph.

userStories.title: The public profile page (/:username) needed 9 requests over 2 serial round trips before it could render
userStories.description: First slice of US-286, which also closes the round-2 finding about open houses. Before this change, every visit to an agent's public page (the link in every Instagram bio) fetched the profiles row first, then fired eight reads keyed on its id: listings, testimonials, links, user_settings, custom_pages, plus the public_agent_response_hours, profile_shows_branding and list_public_open_houses RPCs. Now a SECURITY INVOKER function, get_public_profile_page(_username), returns the same data as one jsonb value. usePublicProfile calls it first, passes the branding flag and open houses to the hooks that own them (setQueryData under their own keys) so those hooks send nothing on mount, and falls back to the old table reads when the function is missing (PGRST202 or 42883), so the frontend can ship before the migration. Open houses are only read when the agent shows listings. Before, the list_public_open_houses prefetch ran even when the section could never mount.
acceptanceCriteria: One network request serves profile + listings + testimonials + links + settings + response hours + custom page + branding + open houses (test: calls === ['rpc:get_public_profile_page'])
Function is SECURITY INVOKER, names only the public profile columns, pins search_path; REVOKE FROM PUBLIC and GRANT to anon/authenticated/service_role; no DEFINER_CALLABLE entry needed
Frontend still works against a database without the function (PGRST202 falls back to the table reads; test)
A null answer is a PGRST116 'Profile not found' error, so FullProfilePage renders NotFound; any other RPC error comes back as an error, with no second attempt
Open houses are neither read nor cached when settings.show_listings is false
check-bundle-size passes; entry chunk +307 B gzip
userStories.notes:
Before and after, for an anonymous /:username visit: before, profiles, then listings, testimonials, links, user_settings, custom_pages and 3 RPCs = 9 requests over 2 serial round trips (src/hooks/usePublicProfile.ts at base: the profiles .single(), then Promise.all plus 2 prefetches). After, get_public_profile_page = 1 request over 1 round trip. The new test src/hooks/usePublicProfile.rpc.test.tsx records the request list for both paths. Entry chunk (index-*.js) measured with vite build before and after: 215,770 B / 61,812 B gzip before, 216,439 B / 62,119 B gzip after (+669 B raw, +307 B gzip). check-bundle-size reports OK.

Files:
- supabase/migrations/20261107000329_public_profile_page_one_round_trip.sql: plpgsql STABLE SECURITY INVOKER function. SET search_path = public, extensions, pg_temp. The columns, filters and ordering match the table reads exactly, including the listings order sort_order, created_at DESC, id (US-253) and the published-or-owner filter (is_published IS TRUE OR id = auth.uid(), US-265). Because it runs as the caller, the US-308 RLS policies and the profiles column grants apply unchanged. It calls the three anon-callable DEFINER helpers that already exist. openHouses is NULL when show_listings is false.
- src/hooks/usePublicProfile.ts:
  - fetchPublicProfilePageRpc returns undefined when the function is missing, so the caller falls back.
  - shapePublicProfilePage is shared by both paths, so the jsonb narrowing and defaults cannot drift between them.
  - seedSideQueries passes branding and open houses to their hooks.
  - fetchPublicProfilePageByTables is the old path, unchanged.
- src/integrations/supabase/types.ts: added get_public_profile_page in the generator's format (Args { _username: string }, Returns Json).
- The tests for the old path (usePublicProfile.test.tsx, usePublicProfile.sideQueries.test.tsx, ProfileRoute.test.tsx) now mock the new RPC as PGRST202, so they still pin the fallback's behaviour.

Not verified: npm run verify:schema needs a live Postgres. psql 16 binaries are present, but this sandbox would not let me start a server (su to postgres was refused). CI's verify-backend job will run it. The checks to watch are the function applying in one pass and 'every rpc() the browser calls is executable by authenticated'; the latter is covered by the GRANT.

userStories.title: Agents could rewrite system-written data in their own notifications (US-322)
userStories.description: Fixes US-322. Before this, an agent could change every column of their own notifications rows. That included the lead_overdue row the overdue-lead chaser treats as "already chased" (US-309). Changing that row's type or data.lead_id makes the chaser email about that lead again, or stops it chasing a different lead. Now the browser can change read_at and nothing else.
acceptanceCriteria: Owner can mark a notification read (UPDATE read_at ... RETURNING id works); UPDATE of type, title, message, data, user_id or created_at is refused with permission denied
anon cannot UPDATE notifications
verify:schema check 'an agent can mark a notification read but not rewrite it' passes with the migration and FAILS (7 findings) when table-wide UPDATE is re-granted
tsc and tests pass
userStories.notes:
Evidence: supabase/migrations/20260806000005_squashed_baseline.sql:14756 has `CREATE POLICY "Users update own notifications" ON public.notifications FOR UPDATE USING ((auth.uid() = user_id))`. It has no TO clause and no column limit, and Supabase's default table-wide UPDATE grant was still in place. The only browser writer is src/hooks/useNotifications.ts:86-108 (markAsRead / markAllAsRead), and it sends only read_at. The chaser's claim is the partial unique index in 20261107000309_lead_overdue_once.sql:25 together with listChasedLeadIds in supabase/functions/scheduled-maintenance/index.ts:55-75, which reads type='lead_overdue' and data.lead_id. Both of those were writable by the owner. data.lead_id is also where the bell sends the agent (src/components/ui/notification-dropdown.tsx:27).

Changes:
- New migration /home/user/plain-page-link/.claude/worktrees/wf_c99d3202-109-6/supabase/migrations/20261107000330_notifications_owner_updates_read_at_only.sql:
  - `REVOKE UPDATE ON public.notifications FROM PUBLIC, anon, authenticated; GRANT UPDATE (read_at) ON public.notifications TO authenticated;`
  - re-creates the policy `TO authenticated` with an explicit WITH CHECK
  - adds a COMMENT on read_at
  - the service role keeps its full grant, so scheduled-maintenance, stripe-webhook and the SECURITY DEFINER notify triggers are unaffected
  - INSERT stays service_role only and there is still no DELETE policy
- /home/user/plain-page-link/.claude/worktrees/wf_c99d3202-109-6/scripts/verify-schema.mjs: new check placed after the US-254 check. It confirms:
  - the owner can mark read, including the `.select('id')` read-back the dashboard uses
  - each of the other 6 columns is refused, and the row's type and data are unchanged afterwards
  - another agent's row is not touched
  - anon is refused
- /home/user/plain-page-link/.claude/worktrees/wf_c99d3202-109-6/src/hooks/useNotifications.test.ts (new): checks that markAsRead and markAllAsRead send only read_at, and that mark-all is limited to the signed-in user. Any other column in the payload would now fail the whole update.

How it was verified: I ran verify:schema end to end against a local Postgres 16 (data directory /var/lib/postgresql/us330, server stopped afterwards). I loaded the prelude, then applied every migration in order with a reconnect between files, then ran the full verify-schema. To prove the new check catches the bug, I re-granted table-wide UPDATE and ran it again: the new check failed and was the only failure. I then restored the migration's grants.

VERIFIED: - `npx tsc --noEmit`: exit 0, no output.
- `npx vitest run src/hooks/useNotifications.test.ts src/components/ui`: 7 files, 29 tests passed.
- `npm run verify:migrations`: "[migrations] OK — 59 migration files structurally valid."
- Local Postgres 16, migrations applied with ON_ERROR_STOP: exit 0, no errors.
- `node scripts/verify-schema.mjs --db-url postgresql://postgres@localhost:55433/agentbio`: exit 0, "All schema checks passed." The new check shows "ok    an agent can mark a notification read but not rewrite it"; 7 expected "permission denied for table notifications" lines are printed above it.
- Negative control (`GRANT UPDATE ON public.notifications TO anon, authenticated`, then verify-schema again): exit 1. Exactly 1 FAIL, the new check, with 7 findings: type, title, message, data and created_at could be updated, the row changed to system_alert|l-9, and anon could update read_at.
- `node scripts/gen-supabase-types.mjs --check`: "types.ts is up to date."

REVIEW: approve

OWNER ACTIONS: Apply migration supabase/migrations/20261107000330_notifications_owner_updates_read_at_only.sql to production. No edge function redeploy is needed.

userStories.title: A missed digest run meant no morning email that day, and agents past the first 1,000 profiles never got one
userStories.description: Fixes US-293. The morning digest now catches up a missed run exactly once, using digest_log to track who has been sent. Each page of profiles is read separately, along with that page's agents' leads, tasks and key dates, so every agent gets a full digest. Failures that used to count as zero or "skipped" are now reported, and they fail the task.
acceptanceCriteria: A run hours after DIGEST_HOUR_UTC, up to DIGEST_CATCHUP_HOURS later (default 6, never past midnight UTC), sends to every agent who has no digest_log row for today; a second run in the window sends nothing (alreadySent)

The look-back windows (new leads 24h, weekly 7d, tasks due) are measured from the scheduled hour, not from when the run happened, so a late edition covers the same leads an on-time one would and tomorrow's edition does not repeat them

Every profile past 5,000 receives its digest: profiles are read 500 at a time with keyset paging, and each page's related rows are read with in(user_id) in groups of 100 ids, paged by 1,000 until the end
A failed weekly count, claim, contact lookup or claim release goes into the report as an error, the digests task fails (207), and it is never read as zero or as skipped
If reading one page fails, that page's agents are counted as failed and later pages still send; the next run in the window sends to the failed page only
userStories.notes:
Evidence (before): supabase/functions/scheduled-maintenance/digests.ts:41 `if (!opts.force && now.getUTCHours() !== hour) return` meant a missed hourly run (GitHub Actions cron, .github/workflows/scheduled-maintenance.yml) lost that day's digest for everyone. digests.ts:52-71 read profiles with `.limit(5000)` (PostgREST's max-rows of 1,000 applies on top of that), and leads/tasks across ALL agents with `.limit(5000)` and contact_key_dates with `.limit(10000)` and no user filter, so agents past those lines got a thinner digest or none. The weekly counts used `count ?? 0` and ignored errors, so a failed count read as zero. Claim errors were logged and counted as skipped, a null contact counted as skipped, and the result of the release delete was never checked.

What changed:
- supabase/functions/scheduled-maintenance/digests.ts is now pure and has no Deno globals, following the overdue.ts/US-309 pattern. digestSchedule(now, {hour, catchUpHours, force}) returns {day, anchor} or null. runDigests(store, {schedule, siteUrl}) pages profiles 500 at a time by keyset (id > afterId) and reads digest_log in bulk to skip agents already sent. It then reads leads, tasks and key dates for the remaining agents in groups of 100 ids, paged by 1,000. It checks the content before looking up the agent's address, then claims, sends, and releases the claim if the send fails. A failed page is counted as failed and the run continues with later pages. summarizeDigestReport gives the one-line result.
- New supabase/functions/scheduled-maintenance/digest-store.ts: supabaseDigestStore(), where every read and write throws on error. The weekly counts are now bounded by the anchor (lt).
- index.ts:200-222 reads DIGEST_HOUR_UTC and DIGEST_CATCHUP_HOURS, runs the schedule, and throws with the summary when report.errors is non-empty, the same as the account_deletions task.
- supabase/functions/.env.example: added DIGEST_CATCHUP_HOURS=6.
- No migration: the catch-up uses the existing digest_log primary key (user_id, digest_date, kind).

Tests: digests.test.ts went from 6 to 24 tests. They use an in-memory store that behaves like the database and cover: 5,200 profiles all sent, with id chunks of 100 or fewer; one agent's 1,005 leads all counted; a missed run caught up exactly once; a late run excluding leads that arrived after the scheduled hour; already-sent agents not looked up again; agents with nothing to send not looked up; a failed page recovered by the next run; a failed send releasing the claim; a failed release reported; a failed weekly count reported as an error rather than zero; an unreadable agent counted as failed while an agent with no address is not; and a source check on the index/store wiring.

VERIFIED: `npx tsc --noEmit`: exit 0, no output. The root tsconfig does not include supabase/functions, so I also ran strict `tsc` (noUnusedLocals/Parameters) on digests.ts, digest-store.ts and index.ts using a throwaway tsconfig that stubs Deno and the esm.sh module: no errors. I deleted that tsconfig afterwards. `npx vitest run supabase/functions/scheduled-maintenance supabase/functions/_shared/digest.test.ts`: 3 files, 48 tests passed, both before and after the pre-commit prettier/eslint reformat. No migration added, so I did not run verify:migrations.

REVIEW: approve

OWNER ACTIONS: Redeploy the edge functions server (functions.agentbio.net, the Coolify app built from the root Dockerfile) so scheduled-maintenance picks up the new digest logic and the new digest-store.ts file | Optional: set DIGEST_CATCHUP_HOURS (default 6) on the functions server. With DIGEST_HOUR_UTC=13 the catch-up window is 13:00 to 19:59 UTC

Evidence for what ships, and what was changed:

- CalendarBooking.tsx: the old page claimed a Google Calendar integration, OAuth, two-way sync, an approval step, a required phone number and "Buyer gets email and SMS reminder" (old line 184). userStories.title: After a deploy, opening the installed app offline on a page the agent had never visited showed a blank screen
userStories.description: Slice for US-321, done as US-334. public/sw.js precached '/index.html' but not the /assets entry files that page loads. After a deploy, if the visitor went offline on a route they had never opened, the worker fell back to that '/index.html'. Its entry chunk had never been downloaded, so the installed app showed a blank screen. At install, the worker now reads the precached '/' and '/index.html' and pulls out the module entry script, the modulepreload links and the stylesheets. It only takes files on its own site under /assets/, and precaches each one. A file that fails to download is skipped, and the install still finishes. On activate, the /assets entries of an old precache are moved into agentbio-sw-runtime-v1 before that precache is deleted. Without this, a page saved under the previous build (the US-312 pages cache) would lose its entry chunks.
acceptanceCriteria: After install, PRECACHE holds index.html plus every /assets file named by its <script type=module>, <link rel=modulepreload> and <link rel=stylesheet> tags. /scripts/*, icons and files from other sites are not taken (tested)
Opening a never-visited route offline gets the shell, and every entry file it names comes from cache (tested)
A file that throws or returns 404 is skipped. The rest of the shell is still precached and the install completes (tested)
A new worker version moves the old precache's /assets entries into the runtime cache before deleting it. The old shell HTML is not moved (tested)
Checked against a real vite build: all 5 entry files in dist/index.html (index js, react-vendor, state-vendor, supabase, index css) are found, and each exists in dist/
userStories.notes:
I picked US-321 over US-323, US-301 and the Login finding because it is the one that breaks offline use outright (a blank screen in the installed app). The others are smaller or cosmetic.

Evidence before the change (public/sw.js at ce412e7):
- APP_SHELL = ['/', '/index.html', '/offline.html', '/manifest.json'] (line 59), and install only ran cache.addAll(APP_SHELL) (lines 141-149).
- networkFirstNavigation falls back to caches.match('/index.html') (line 261). That page names /assets/index-*.js and the vendor modulepreloads, none of which were precached.

Changes:
- /home/user/plain-page-link/.claude/worktrees/wf_c99d3202-109-10/public/sw.js
  - shellAssetsFromHtml(html, origin): a service worker has no DOMParser, so it reads the script and link tags with a regex. It accepts double-quoted, single-quoted and unquoted attribute values. It only keeps URLs on the same site under /assets/, drops duplicates, and stops at 40 (MAX_SHELL_ASSETS).
  - precacheShellAssets(cache): fetches and stores each file on its own, inside a try. Only ok responses are stored.
  - Install now runs addAll(APP_SHELL), then precacheShellAssets, with failures caught, then skipWaiting.
  - adoptPrecachedAssets(old): in activate, for any agentbio-sw-precache-* being deleted, copies its /assets entries into RUNTIME. It skips entries RUNTIME already has, and the existing trim on activate keeps RUNTIME within its cap.
- /home/user/plain-page-link/.claude/worktrees/wf_c99d3202-109-10/src/sw.test.ts
  - The test harness now takes an optional shell-HTML map for FakeCache.addAll, and its fake fetch accepts a string URL.
  - Added 4 tests in 'precaching the shell entry files (US-321)'.
  - Before committing, I put back the old sw.js and ran the suite: all 4 new tests failed, so they really test the change.

Committed in the worktree only. Not pushed; I did not edit prd.json or progress.txt. lint-staged ran eslint and prettier at commit, and I re-ran tsc and the sw tests after that.

userStories.title: The lead timeline's system rows (status changes, lead created) can no longer be forged, rewritten or deleted through the API
userStories.description: Closes US-335 and US-313, and the round-3 finding about the UPDATE policy. Before this change, a lead owner or assignee could use the shipped anon key and their own session to do three things. (1) Forge 'status_change' or 'form_submission' rows, through log_lead_activity or by inserting directly. (2) Delete the real system rows, because those rows carry the owner's user_id. userStories.title: An agent could rewrite their own pending account-deletion row and use it to switch billing back on for another customer's Stripe subscription
userStories.description:
This follows up the round-3 finding that other baseline `FOR UPDATE USING (owner)` policies might let owners rewrite columns the system writes. I swept the owner UPDATE policies; the worst case is `account_deletion_scheduled`.

Baseline policy `"Users can cancel own deletion"` (squashed_baseline.sql:13974) has no TO clause and no WITH CHECK. Table-wide UPDATE is still granted to the browser roles. So while a deletion is pending, the owner could rewrite any column.

Through PostgREST, an agent could:
1. Request deletion.
2. Set `stripe_subscription_id` to another customer's sub id and `prior_cancel_at_period_end` to false.
3. Cancel the deletion.

On cancel, gdpr-deletion (index.ts:166-192) reads that row. `restoreBillingAfterCancel` (_shared/account-deletion.ts) then uses the platform Stripe key to switch renewal back on for that subscription. A customer who had chosen to leave keeps being charged.

The same policy also let the owner repoint `gdpr_request_id`. `process_scheduled_account_deletions()` marks that request completed, so this could close another user's GDPR request.

`gdpr_data_requests` had the same problem. The owner could insert rows, including one already marked completed with any `file_url`, and could rewrite pending rows. It is the compliance record for subject access and erasure requests.

Nothing in `src/` writes either table. All writes go through SECURITY DEFINER functions (`request_account_deletion`, `cancel_account_deletion`, `request_gdpr_data_export`) or the service role.
acceptanceCriteria: anon/authenticated cannot INSERT, UPDATE, DELETE or TRUNCATE account_deletion_scheduled or gdpr_data_requests; the owner still SELECTs their own rows
The owner write policies 'Users can cancel own deletion', 'Users can cancel own pending GDPR requests' and 'Users can create own GDPR requests' are dropped
cancel_account_deletion (via gdpr-deletion) still cancels a schedule
restoreBillingAfterCancel leaves Stripe alone when the subscription id on the schedule row is not on the caller's own user_subscriptions row
verify:schema has a check covering all of the above; npm run verify:migrations passes
userStories.notes:
Changes:
- New migration /home/user/plain-page-link/.claude/worktrees/wf_c12867ba-1a3-6/supabase/migrations/20261107000353_deletion_schedule_system_written.sql. It revokes INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE/TRUNCATE on both tables from PUBLIC, anon and authenticated. TRUNCATE is included because RLS does not apply to it. It drops the three owner write policies and adds table comments. The SELECT policies and the service_role manage policies are unchanged; gdpr-deletion's GET reads the row with the caller's JWT.
- A second lock in code, in supabase/functions/_shared/account-deletion.ts `restoreBillingAfterCancel`: it now requires the subscription id to be in `store.liveSubscriptionIds(userId)`. Otherwise it logs, returns `unchanged` and never calls Stripe.
- New test in supabase/functions/_shared/account-deletion.test.ts: "refuses to switch renewal back on for a subscription that is not the user's". The existing "restored" test now gives the user that subscription on their row.
- New check in scripts/verify-schema.mjs: "the deletion schedule and GDPR requests are not writable by their subject". It covers the owner trying each sensitive column, plus direct INSERT and DELETE, a GDPR insert born 'completed', a GDPR UPDATE, anon UPDATE, and that cancelling through `cancel_account_deletion` still works.

Not verified live: I could not run verify:schema here. The sandbox refuses `su`/`runuser` and initdb will not run as root, so there was no local Postgres. CI verify-backend.yml will run the new check.

The rest of the sweep, for the record:
- Every other owner UPDATE policy reaches only the agent's own data, with no cross-tenant effect: listings, testimonials, profiles counters, user_sessions, lead_scores, ml_model_weights, mortgage_calculations.

userStories.title: Digest catch-up runs re-read every profile each hour after everyone was already sent (US-344)
userStories.description: After a complete digest pass with no errors, the job now writes one digest_runs row for that day. Later hourly runs in the catch-up window that day return before they read any profile. Before this, each of those runs re-read every profile, every digest_log row, all new leads, due tasks and key dates. On Mondays it also ran three count queries per agent. - supabase/functions/scheduled-maintenance/digests.ts:
  - DigestStore has two new methods, hasCompletedRun(day) and markRunCompleted(day, totals). DigestReport has a new field, skipped.
  - runDigests takes a new option, useRunMarker. When it is on, the job checks the marker before the profile loop and returns skipped=true if the day is already done.
  - After the loop it writes the marker only when errors is empty and failed is 0.
  - If the marker cannot be read, the job still does the full pass. digest_log still prevents a double send, and the read failure is reported as an error.
  - If the marker cannot be written, that is reported as an error after every email has gone out.

- supabase/functions/scheduled-maintenance/index.ts: passes useRunMarker: body.force_digest !== true. A forced run may anchor on now, before the digest hour, so it never records a marker that would block the on-time edition.

userStories.title: Blog article JSON-LD named the social banner as AgentBio's logo, and AgentBio's entity ids were spelled two ways
userStories.description:
Closes US-346. Every blog article's BlogPosting.publisher.logo was set to /Cover.png, which is the 1536x1024 social banner. The site's Organization node uses /logo.png at 946x436. The publisher is now built by one shared helper. It uses the same Organization @id, name, url and measured logo ImageObject as the Organization node.

The same new module, src/config/site-entities.ts, also builds the Organization and WebSite node ids (${origin}/#organization and ${origin}/#website) for every generator that names them. PageSEO and SchemaMarkup had been writing them without the slash before the #.

seo-audit.mjs gets two new rules:
- A logo field may not point at the social banner.
- An entity id (one with a #fragment) may not be written two different ways on one page.
acceptanceCriteria: BlogPosting publisher.logo is deep-equal to the Organization node's logo (/logo.png, 946x436), never /Cover.png
The BlogPosting publisher carries the Organization @id ${origin}/#organization
Organization and WebSite ids are built in one place (site-entities.ts) and spelled ${origin}/#organization and ${origin}/#website everywhere
seo-audit flags a logo that names /Cover.png(.webp), and flags one entity id written two ways on a page
A source guard fails if `}#organization`, `.net#organization` or the #website forms come back anywhere under src/
tsc passes; the related vitest suites pass
userStories.notes:
Defect: src/components/blog/ArticleSEO.tsx:84-91 (before) set publisher.logo.url to `${siteUrl}/Cover.png`. The Organization nodes (src/lib/seo.ts:183, PageSEO.tsx:59) use ORGANIZATION_LOGO, which is /logo.png at 946x436.

Changes:
- New src/config/site-entities.ts with organizationId(), websiteId(), organizationLogo() and publisherOrganization(). Each strips a trailing slash from the origin.
- ArticleSEO.tsx: publisher is now publisherOrganization(siteUrl). This page is live on every /blog/:slug.
- src/lib/seo.ts: the Organization @id and logo now come from the helper. The ProfessionalService logo (generateEnhancedLocalBusinessSchema, rendered by Landing.tsx) now states its width and height; it had stated neither. The SoftwareApplication publisher now refers to the Organization by @id and includes the logo.
- PageSEO.tsx and SchemaMarkup.tsx: ids now use the slash form, and the SchemaMarkup article publisher uses the helper. Both components are currently imported by nothing in src, so in practice the id-spelling split was in unused code. They are aligned so that whoever revives them does not bring it back.
- scripts/lib/seo-audit.mjs: two new rules inside auditStructuredData. (1) A node whose logo points at /Cover.png or /Cover.webp is reported. (2) Every @id containing a # on the page is grouped by new URL().href, and any group with more than one raw spelling is reported. Ids without a # are deliberately left out, so breadcrumb rungs such as `https://agentbio.net` against `https://agentbio.net/` do not trip the build gate.

Tests:
- src/config/site-entities.test.tsx renders ArticleSEO and PageSEO through HelmetProvider in server mode (canUseDOM=false). It checks that publisher.logo deep-equals generateEnhancedOrganizationSchema().logo, that the publisher @id matches the Organization @id, and that every PageSEO reference resolves to an id declared on the page. It also includes the source-scan guard.
- scripts/lib/seo-audit.test.ts has a new 'site entity identity' describe block with two failing and two passing cases.

userStories.title: A failed sign-in on a flaky phone connection reloaded the page and wiped the login form whenever the browser held any cache the app does not own
userStories.description: This closes US-347. `cleanupServiceWorkers` now returns three separate facts: how many legacy workers it unregistered, how many caches it deleted, and whether a worker other than /sw.js still controls the page. `cleanupAndReload` now reloads in only two cases: it unregistered a legacy worker, or one still controls the page. A legacy worker can still control the page when App.tsx has already unregistered it on mount, because unregistering does not release a page that worker already controls. Deleting a stray cache, or finding nothing to clean, no longer reloads, so a failed sign-in on a flaky connection keeps what was typed into the form. The Login toast now says the sign-in service could not be reached, instead of blaming the browser cache.
acceptanceCriteria: cleanupServiceWorkers reports separately whether it unregistered a worker and whether it deleted caches
Login reloads only after it unregistered a legacy worker (or one still controls the page)
Tested in src/lib/sw-cleanup.test.ts
userStories.notes:
The bug: in the old src/lib/sw-cleanup.ts (lines 44-55), cleanedUp was set to true whenever any cache name lacked the 'agentbio-sw-' prefix. src/pages/auth/Login.tsx (lines 139-141) then called cleanupAndReload 3 seconds after every sign-in network error, which reloaded the page.

What changed:
- /home/user/plain-page-link/.claude/worktrees/wf_c12867ba-1a3-10/src/lib/sw-cleanup.ts now returns a `ServiceWorkerCleanupResult` with three fields: `unregisteredWorkers`, `controlledByLegacyWorker` and `deletedCaches`.
- It adds `cleanupNeedsReload(result)`, which is true when a worker was unregistered or a legacy worker still controls the page.
- `cleanupAndReload()` now returns a boolean saying whether it reloaded, and reloads only when `cleanupNeedsReload` is true.
- The scan also checks the waiting and installing script URLs, not just the active one.
- The caller in src/App.tsx:160 ignores the return value, so it needed no change.
- /home/user/plain-page-link/.claude/worktrees/wf_c12867ba-1a3-10/src/pages/auth/Login.tsx has new toast copy and a comment; the 3-second timer is kept.
- /home/user/plain-page-link/.claude/worktrees/wf_c12867ba-1a3-10/src/lib/sw-cleanup.test.ts now has 8 tests. They cover: a foreign cache is deleted with no reload; nothing to clean means no reload; a legacy worker is unregistered and the page reloads; a page still controlled by a legacy worker reloads; and the failure path.

I chose this over US-323 and US-301 because it causes data loss (typed form input) on a core flow.

userStories.title: Listing pages were in no sitemap, so crawlers could not find them
userStories.description: US-358 slice (recorded as US-372). /sitemap-profiles.xml now lists each published agent's visible listing pages (/:username/listing/:id) right after the agent's own URL, with <lastmod> taken from listings.updated_at. Listings hidden by show_listings, and sold listings hidden by show_sold_properties, are left out by reusing selectListingForPage, the same rule the listing page applies. If any of the three anon reads (profiles, listings, user_settings) fails, the sitemap answers 503 instead of a partial list. Decision on prerender: listing pages are not prerendered. Their crawler half is the request-time Pages Function functions/[username]/listing/[listingId].ts, the same way profiles are served, so a build-time file would only go stale.
acceptanceCriteria: The sitemap emits one <url> per visible listing, with lastmod taken from listings.updated_at (only when it parses as a date)
Listings hidden by show_listings or show_sold_properties are not emitted; agents with no user_settings row default to showing everything, as the profile page does
A failed listings or settings read gives a 503, never a sitemap that guesses visibility
The sitemap tests cover it
userStories.notes:
What changed:
- functions/_lib/profile-sitemap.ts: the route reads three tables in parallel with the anon key:
  - profiles?select=id,username&is_published=is.true&order=username.asc
  - listings?select=id,user_id,status,updated_at&status=in.(active,pending,under_contract,sold)&order=id.asc
  - user_settings?select=user_id,show_listings,show_sold_properties&order=user_id.asc
  Each read is paged by 1000 through a shared fetchAllRows helper. The new sitemapEntries() places each agent's visible listings right after the agent's URL, using listingPagePath from src/lib/listingShare.ts and selectListingForPage from src/lib/publicListingVisibility.ts. Listing entries have priority 0.5 and profile entries 0.6. The whole list is still capped at MAX_URLS (50,000).
- src/lib/publicListingVisibility.ts:10: the import of listingStatus is now relative instead of '@/'. The Pages Functions bundle does not resolve the Vite alias, and functions/ already imports src/lib this way (profile-sitemap.ts → ../../src/lib/username). I checked by hand that listingStatus, listingShare and username import nothing else.
- functions/_tests/sitemap-profiles.test.ts: the fetch stub now answers by table name, because the reads run in parallel. The US-262 cases are kept. New cases cover: listing ordering and lastmod, the query shape for listings and settings, both visibility toggles, a 503 on a failed listings or settings read, drafts and unknown agents, reserved usernames, encoding, and duplicate rows.

Why the schema allows these reads:
- The anon SELECT policy on listings (migration 20261107000308:50-61) already limits rows to public statuses, NOT is_sample, and published agents. There is no column grant on listings, so updated_at is readable.
- Anon is granted SELECT on exactly user_id, show_listings and show_sold_properties on user_settings, for published agents only (20260902000009). user_id is unique (baseline:8203), so it is safe to order the paging by it.
- profiles.id is among the anon-granted columns.

userStories.title: Logged meetings did not count as first contact (closes US-336)
userStories.description: Agents use the "Log meeting" form on a lead to record a meeting. It saved the meeting to the timeline, but it never set leads.contacted_at. So a lead whose first contact was a meeting still showed as never contacted, and the response-time numbers counted it as unanswered. Meetings now go through a new SECURITY DEFINER RPC, log_lead_meeting. It works the same way as log_lead_call and log_lead_email: only the lead's owner or current assignee can call it, the row is saved under the caller's id, and contacted_at is set once and never moved after that.
acceptanceCriteria: Logging a meeting on an uncontacted lead sets leads.contacted_at; a later meeting does not move it (log_lead_meeting uses COALESCE(contacted_at, NOW()); verify-schema check 'log_lead_meeting records the meeting and first contact')
useLeadActivities.logMeeting calls supabase.rpc('log_lead_meeting') and no longer inserts into lead_activities (hook test src/hooks/useLeadActivities.meeting.test.ts)
Only the lead owner or its current assignee can log a meeting. A stranger is refused, and so is a meeting type outside in_person/video/phone
The function pins search_path = public, extensions, pg_temp. EXECUTE is revoked from PUBLIC/anon/authenticated and granted to authenticated and service_role. It is listed in DEFINER_CALLABLE
userStories.notes:
Evidence: before this change, src/hooks/useLeadActivities.ts:251-270 (logMeetingMutation) wrote straight to the table with supabase.from('lead_activities').insert({... activity_type: 'meeting' ...}) and never touched leads.contacted_at. Every other contact path does set it: log_lead_call, log_lead_email, and log_lead_activity for email/call/meeting/sms (supabase/migrations/20261107000326_assignee_logs_lead_activity.sql, 20261107000349_...sql). log_lead_activity could not be reused because it has no parameters for meeting_type, meeting_location or meeting_scheduled_at.

Changes:
- supabase/migrations/20261107000373_log_lead_meeting.sql: new public.log_lead_meeting(_lead_id uuid, _meeting_type text, _location text, _scheduled_at timestamptz, _notes text). It rejects an unknown meeting_type with check_violation, then applies the owner-or-current-assignee guard. It inserts the meeting row with user_id = auth.uid(), the meeting columns, is_internal=false and metadata, and sets contacted_at = COALESCE(contacted_at, NOW()). It follows the REVOKE/GRANT pattern in CLAUDE.md.
- src/hooks/useLeadActivities.ts: logMeeting calls the RPC. Its onSuccess still refreshes ['leads'], so the lead stops showing as uncontacted.
- src/integrations/supabase/types.ts: added the Functions.log_lead_meeting Args/Returns entry by hand, in the format the generator uses.
- scripts/verify-schema.mjs: added log_lead_meeting to DEFINER_CALLABLE, plus a new real-Postgres check. The check confirms that an unknown type and a stranger are refused, that a refused call leaves contacted_at unset, that the assignee can log a meeting, that the row lands with the right user_id and meeting details, that contacted_at is set, and that a later meeting from the owner does not move it.
- Tests: src/hooks/useLeadActivities.meeting.test.ts covers the exact RPC arguments, that nothing calls insert, the refresh of ['leads'], optional fields passed as undefined, and the error toast on refusal. src/lib/leadMeetingFirstContact.test.ts checks the migration text: the guard, the definer search_path, the grants, the DEFINER_CALLABLE entry, that this is the latest definition, and that the hook no longer inserts.

Not run: verify:schema and types:check against a real database. Postgres refuses to start as root, and starting it as the postgres user (su/runuser) was blocked by the worktree isolation guard. CI's verify-backend job runs both.

userStories.title: Agents can upload a brokerage logo instead of typing a URL (closes US-280)
userStories.description: The profile editor's free-text "Brokerage Logo URL" field is gone. The logo is now uploaded into the brokerage-logos bucket, with a preview and Replace and Remove buttons. The avatar and the logo share one upload hook, useProfileImageUpload. That hook also fixes an ordering bug: the avatar upload used to delete the old image before the new one was in place.

The URL text input is removed from src/pages/dashboard/Profile.tsx

userStories.notes:
Evidence before the change: src/pages/dashboard/Profile.tsx (around 580-595, at HEAD a08504b) took brokerage_logo as `<input type="url">`. That meant hot-linked, unvalidated third-party images on the public page, and most agents have no hosted URL to give. Migration 20260808000005 already creates a public 'brokerage-logos' bucket (2MB, no SVG) with owner-scoped write policies keyed on the first path segment, which is the user's id. - Bug fixed along the way: useAvatarUpload used to delete every object in the folder before uploading. A failed upload or profile update therefore left avatar_url pointing at a deleted file. The shared hook deletes only after the profile points at the new file.
- src/hooks/useAvatarUpload.ts is now a thin wrapper. It keeps its return shape { uploadAvatar, uploading, acceptedTypes, maxSize }, so its callers are unchanged.
- New src/hooks/useBrokerageLogoUpload.ts: brokerage-logos bucket, column brokerage_logo, prefix 'logo', 2MB.
- Profile.tsx, Professional tab:
  - logo preview with a fixed-size frame and an ImagePlus placeholder
  - Upload/Replace and Remove buttons, both 44px touch targets
  - help text tied to the button with aria-describedby
  - a hidden file input, cleared after each pick so picking the same file again still works
  - an upload saves immediately and does not show as an unsaved change, like the avatar; Remove is a normal form edit that Save sends as brokerage_logo: ''
- No migration is needed.

userStories.title: vite.config.ts was never type-checked: tsconfig.node.json failed and CI never ran it (US-365)
userStories.description: Completes US-365. vite.config.ts sets the vendor chunks and stamps the service worker version, but nothing type-checked it. The root tsconfig.json includes only src and functions. `tsc -p tsconfig.node.json` failed with TS6307: the composite project did not list the src/config files that vite.config.ts imports. It also failed with TS18028 on vitest .d.ts files, because no target was set. CI never ran that command. tsconfig.node.json is now a strict no-emit project and CI runs it.
acceptanceCriteria: npx tsc --noEmit -p tsconfig.node.json exits 0
CI runs it (.github/workflows/ci.yml typecheck job, step 'Type check build config')
npx tsc --noEmit (root) still exits 0
An error in vite.config.ts or in an imported src/config module makes the check fail
userStories.notes:
What changed:
- tsconfig.node.json: dropped composite and noEmit:false. Now noEmit:true, target and lib ES2022, skipLibCheck, strict, noUnusedLocals, noUnusedParameters, types ["node"]. The include list stays vite.config.ts and vitest.config.ts. Without composite, imported files such as src/config/{homepage-seo,sw-version,vendor-chunks}.ts are pulled in automatically, so they do not need to be listed. A future ./src/config import also cannot bring back TS6307.
- tsconfig.json: removed `references: [{ path: ./tsconfig.node.json }]`. It is a Vite-template leftover that does nothing for `tsc --noEmit` without -b. Once the node project shares src/config files with the root project, keeping the reference makes the root tsc fail with TS6305 (it asks for built .d.ts files). userStories.title: Hashed chunks and PWA icons were sent two conflicting cache policies, so neither the asset year nor any icon policy worked as written (closes US-301)
userStories.description:
I took US-301, the open mobile slice for unhashed icons cached as immutable. Looking into it turned up a bigger fault underneath. Cloudflare Pages does not let a later _headers rule win. It applies every matching rule and joins a header that two rules both set with a comma. This is in the Cloudflare docs and in workers-sdk pages-shared/asset-server/handler.ts, which calls headers.append. public/_headers and scripts/check-route-weight.mjs both assumed "later rule wins". So production sent these values:
- /assets/* chunks, /icons/* and the root brand images: `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate, public, max-age=31536000, immutable`. A cache uses the first max-age, so the immutable year never applied.
- /sw.js: three Cache-Control policies, and `application/javascript` sent twice.
The route-weight budget meanwhile measured a clean year. Fix: each rule that replaces the floor now detaches the inherited value first with `! Cache-Control`. Only /assets/* is immutable. Unhashed public images get max-age=86400, so a new icon reaches returning visitors and installed PWAs. /sw.js and /scripts/* revalidate on every load. The parser now follows Pages' rules, and tests check the resolved headers for every file in public/.
acceptanceCriteria: /icons/* and the root-level brand images (Icon, logo, Cover, placeholder-property.svg) resolve to Cache-Control `public, max-age=86400`, with no immutable
/assets/* (js, css, png, webp, woff2) resolves to exactly `public, max-age=31536000, immutable`, and no file in public/ gets immutable
/sw.js and /scripts/* resolve to exactly `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate`; /sw.js Content-Type is sent once
No deployed path is sent more than one max-age directive or a comma-joined Content-Type
scripts/check-route-weight.mjs resolves _headers the way Pages does (append, `! Name` detach, :placeholder), and the budget refuses to run unless hashed assets resolve to exactly the immutable year
deployed-files.test.ts holds all of the above for every file in public/
userStories.notes:
Evidence:
- Cloudflare docs (pages/configuration/headers.mdx, line 60): "If a header is applied twice in the _headers file, the values are joined with a comma separator". Line 62 covers "Detach a header" with `! Name`.
- workers-sdk packages/pages-shared/asset-server/handler.ts:525-537 applies the matched rules in order: delete the detached headers, then headers.append when an earlier rule already set that name.
- workers-shared parseHeaders.ts:121 parses `! Name` into unsetHeaders.
- I resolved the old public/_headers (git HEAD) with the corrected parser:
  - /assets/a.js got `public, max-age=0, must-revalidate, public, max-age=31536000, immutable`
  - /icons/icon-192.png got the same
  - /sw.js got three policies and `application/javascript, application/javascript`
  - After the change each of these resolves to one clean value.

Changes:
- public/_headers:
  - The floor comment now explains the joining behaviour.
  - The cache section is rewritten. Extension rules carry only Content-Type, except images, which detach and set max-age=86400.
  - New /assets/* rule detaches and sets the immutable year.
  - /*.html sets only Content-Type.
  - /scripts/* and /sw.js detach and restate revalidate. /sw.js no longer sets Content-Type a second time.
  - Each path appears only once, because Pages keys rules by path.
- scripts/check-route-weight.mjs:
  - parseHeaders(source?) also records `unset`.
  - matches() supports :placeholder.
  - headersFor() appends, and honours detach.
  - main() requires the exact year string.
- scripts/check-route-weight.d.mts: types updated to match.
- src/deployed-files.test.ts: the position-based checks, which relied on "later wins", are replaced by resolved-header checks over every public/ file plus sample /assets paths.
- src/route-weight.test.ts: added tests for the semantics (join, detach, placeholder).

Not run: the route-weight budget itself (npm run route-weight). It needs a build and Chromium. In CI it should now measure real production headers.

userStories.title: If one app-shell file fails during service worker install, the installed app loses its offline fallback until the next deploy
userStories.description: public/sw.js:226-238: cache.addAll(APP_SHELL) succeeds or fails as a whole, and the error is swallowed before skipWaiting. If '/', '/index.html', '/offline.html' or '/manifest.json' fails once on a flaky phone connection, the new precache is left empty. activate (lines 241-262) then deletes the previous, working precache. Offline navigation to a route the visitor never opened then returns the plain-text 503. Fix: cache each shell entry on its own; if '/index.html' and '/offline.html' are missing from the new precache, copy them from the previous precache before deleting it.
